items.title: Nová koncepce má pomoci zlepšit podmínky pro stromy v centru Brna
items.summary_raw: Vytvářet lepší podmínky pro stávající i nové stromy při obnově ulic a veřejných prostranství v historickém jádru Brna má pomoct nová koncepce. Klade důraz například na dostatek místa pro růst kořenů nebo na lepší využívání dešťové vody. Dokument, který zpracovala Kancelář architekta města Brna, už schválili radní. Koncepce bude účinná od února příštího roku, uvedl magistrát.

items.title: Hypotéky míří k šesti procentům. Může to zpomalit růst cen starších bytů a pro kupující vytvořit prostor pro vyjednání slev
items.summary_raw: Největší slevové příležitosti budou v dohledné době u „ležáků“, tedy nemovitostí, o něž z různých důvodů není mezi kupujícími příliš velký zájem. Dopad na trh s novostavbami bude podle expertů menší.

items.title: Jsme rozmazlení. Doprava podraží a lidé už nebudou mít zboží druhý den doma, říká manažer největší dopravní firmy na světě
items.summary_raw: Podle Tomáše Holomouckého, ředitele DSV Contract Logistics, je svět od covidu složitější, více turbulentní a křehčí ve všech ohledech. Zásadní je geopolitika, které dříve logistické firmy nemusely dávat v plánování téměř žádnou váhu. Nyní...

items.title: Darovat plazmu se dá i mimo velká města. Třeba v Kladně nebo v Táboře
items.summary_raw: Odběrová centra fungovala dlouho hlavně v krajských městech. Dnes jich má například jen UNICAplasma 8. Patří mezi ně Praha, Ostrava, Český Těšín, Frýdek-Místek, 2 pobočky v Českých Budějovicích, a mezi žádané lokality patří také Kladno a Tábor.

items.title: Stovky zpráv denně a další povinnosti na obzoru. Jednotné hlášení firmám úlevu nepřineslo, od listopadu hrozí pokuty
items.summary_raw: Dřívějších 25 formulářů, které zaměstnavatelé museli povinně a pravidelně posílat různým úřadům, nahradil letos na jaře jeden jediný. Má jít o úlevu pro firmy od administrativy, ale realita za očekáváním zatím pokulhává. Takzvané jednotné měsíční...

items.title: Překoná bitcoin už příští rok rekord 126 tisíc dolarů? K dalšímu růstu může přispět i zadlužení USA
items.summary_raw: Ještě na začátku loňského října se bitcoin obchodoval na rekordních hodnotách. V jednu chvíli nejznámější kryptoměna dokonce překonala hranici 126 tisíc dolarů. Ve stejném měsíci ale došlo k prudkému propadu a likvidaci pákových pozic v hodnotě 19...

items.title: Zrcadlovky mají utrum. Nový supertelefon boří veškeré limity
items.summary_raw: Vivo přináší novou řadu vlajkových smartphonů X500 Pro a X500 Pro Max. Tyto modely definitivně mění pravidla mobilní fotografie. Přináší unikátní 200Mpx teleobjektiv, natáčení videa ve filmové kvalitě a revoluční 2nm procesor s obrovským výkonem.

items.title: Podle čeho poznat dobrou telemedicínu? Ti, kdo platí, se začínají ptát
items.summary_raw: Telemedicína v Česku dospěla. Využívají ji jednotlivci, ale i kraje, zaměstnavatelé nebo pojišťovny. Nejde už jen o to, zda konzultace na dálku funguje, ale podle čeho poznat, že funguje dobře. Plátci, kterým letos ubývají rezervy, se ptají na odpovědnost, jména lékařů, certifikované technologie a hlavně na čísla, která lze doložit.

items.title: Top 10 událostí z energetiky za poslední týden
items.summary_raw: Tento týden vám opět přinášíme pečlivě vybraný seznam deseti nejvýznamnějších článků, které jsme publikovali na webu oEnergetice.cz. Pokud jste kterýkoliv článek nestihli, zde je výběr článků, které zaujaly naše čtenáře nejvíc. Hodně štěstí do nového týdne! 1. Německo ruší povinné plnění plynových zásobníků. Vzniknout má národní rezerva Německo podle návrhu ministerstva hospodářství a energetiky hodlá do […]

items.title: Zelenskyj obvinil Trumpa, že tlačí Ukrajinu, aby se vzdala Rusku
items.summary_raw: Donald Trump měl naléhat na ukrajinského prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského, aby se jeho země vzdala Rusku. Zelenskyj zároveň údajně předložil návrh, v němž by vyhověl Trumpovu požadavku a zastavil útoky na ruské rafinerie.

items.title: Násilí, rabování, hořící budovy. Ve Francii to vře, Macron slíbil tvrdě zakročit
items.summary_raw: Ve Francii v sobotu protestovaly stovky tisíc lidí proti vysokým životním nákladům. Protesty se zvrhly ve střety s policií, rabování či útoky na úřady. Policie zadržela přes dva tisíce lidí. Prezident slíbil potrestání viníků nepokojů, chce ale jednat se studentskými organizacemi.

items.title: Zemřel herec, moderátor a výtvarník Otakar Jirák. Bylo mu 77 let
items.summary_raw: Otakar Jirák ztvárnil desítky rolí ve filmech i seriálech. Dětští diváci ho mohli znát jako dabéra postavičky Hele z televizního Studia Kamarád.

items.title: Máme AI agenty pod kontrolou? Koubský a Zandl: Jejich cílem je plnit zadání. Jsou to jedničky a nuly
items.summary_raw: V polovině července se ukázalo, že AI agenti dokážou obejít bezpečnostní opatření, uniknout z uzavřeného testovacího rozhraní a proniknout na servery nic netušících společností. „Nastala spíše lidská chyba v zadání,“ míní o známém případu Hugging Face publicista a provozovatel webu vibecoding.cz Patrick Zandl. „Myslím, že jsme v tomhle směru daleko odolnější, než si myslíme,“ říká v pořadu Online Plus redaktor Deníku N Petr Koubský.

items.title: Pastevec z Domažlicka udržuje se stádem jaků, ovcí a koz bezlesí v Českém lese
items.summary_raw: Pastevci rodiny Františka Groessla z Českého svazu ochránců přírody Libosváry z Domažlicka udržují se stádem zhruba 250 jaků, ovcí a koz velmi cenná bezlesí v Českém lese. Pro chráněnou krajinnou oblast Český les (CHKO) je jejich činnost zásadní, řekl ČTK ředitel správy CHKO Tomáš Peckert. Groessl, který už sepsal troje Pastevcovy zápisky, uvedl že je v oblasti jediný, kdo se pastevectvím snaží zachovat na Domažlicku a Tachovsku více než deset přírodně jedinečných lokalit.

items.title: V Indii byl po 150 letech znovu spatřen vzácný šípovec africký
items.summary_raw: Po více než 150 letech byl v Indii spatřen šípovec africký (Psammophis schokari). Hada zaznamenal minulý měsíc v indické oblasti Kaččh v západním státě Gudžarát lesní strážce Džajéš Dumadija, informoval deník Indian Express. Tento druh v oblasti viděl naposledy v roce 1872 český přírodovědec Ferdinand Stolička, který zde sbíral zoologické vzorky.

items.title: Zpívající lemuři používají stejné triky jako sopranistky
items.summary_raw: Když operní pěvkyně zpívají vysoké tóny, může i nepatrná úprava tvaru úst a hrdla zajistit, že se zvuk rozlehne do větší dálky. Podle nejnovějších výzkumů by zpívající lemuři, jedno z nejneobvyklejších zvířat Madagaskaru, mohli v korunách stromů dělat něco podobného, píše agentura Reuters.

items.title: V Přerově spojí síly ANO, ODS a lidovci. Primátorem by měl zůstat Vrána
items.summary_raw: Stejně jako v uplynulých čtyřech letech by v Přerově měla vzniknout koalice na půdorysu ANO, ODS a lidovců. V křesle primátora má setrvat Petr Vrána z vítězného ANO.

items.title: Video: Blízká setkání s vraky i starou silnicí. Projít si teď Slapy je zážitek
items.summary_raw: Hladina Slapské přehrady klesá o více než metr týdně a odhaluje tak místa, která byla celá desetiletí skrytá. Redaktoři Seznam Zpráv zmapovali úseky, kde ustupující hladina odkryla nečekané nálezy i kus zapomenuté historie.

items.title: Zemanovi jsme se s kolegy smáli, Klaus mě chválil, říká bývalý zpravodaj BBC
items.summary_raw: BBC se v červnu rozhodla zrušit 2000 pracovních míst, včetně pozic pěti evropských zpravodajů. Končí i Rob Cameron pokrývající Česko a Slovensko. V rozhovoru říká, že jde BBC sama proti sobě, a vzpomíná na reportování z Česka.

items.title: Těžký týden: Volební discopříběh s kolonoskopií

items.title: Senátorský klub Starostů opět povede znovuzvolený Sobotka

items.title: Bytová výstavba v Česku prudce roste. Menší developeři ale narážejí na problém
items.summary_raw: Počet zahájených bytů v Česku v srpnu meziročně vzrostl o 42 procent, přestože stavebnictví jako celek oslabilo. Oživení výstavby nemusí znamenat stejné příležitosti pro všechny developery. Rozhoduje především dostupnost financování. Alternativní kapitál může pomoci menším firmám rozjet nové projekty. Jeho využívání ale přináší také rizika.

items.title: Podpora Ukrajiny se příští rok může rozpadnout, varuje slavný politolog
items.summary_raw: Otevřené hranice v Evropě nám přinesly to nejlepší i to nejhorší, říká slavný bulharský politolog Ivan Krastev. Viděli jsme do té doby netušené příležitosti, ale viděli jsme také naše přátele odcházet.

items.title: Pomoc téměř neexistuje. Dítě s autismem je v péči dvě stě kilometrů od rodičů
items.summary_raw: Mít dítě s těžkým autismem v Česku často znamená zůstat na všechno úplně sám, shodují se rodiče. Popisují přetížené nebo zcela neexistující služby, mnohaleté pořadníky i umístění dítěte do zařízení daleko od domova.

items.title: Čínská sázka na štědrost, varování pro Česko a odvrácená tvář Polska
items.summary_raw: Pouhá reklama už nestačí, čínské automobilky expandují v Česku prostřednictvím širšího sponzorství. Na českém finančním trhu se od konce srpna odehrává neobvyklý souběh událostí. Polský zlotý dramaticky oslabuje, problémy Polska jsou čím dál tíživější i v Česku. Přečtěte si nejzajímavější články tohoto týdne.

items.title: „Plakal jsem. Rozprášili mou oblast výzkumu.“ Začala revoluce v matematice
items.summary_raw: AI se pustila do matematiky. OpenAI zveřejnila stovky nových důkazů. Vyřešila matematické problémy, které zatím žádný člověk vyřešit nedokázal. Ale mnozí experti místo oslav bijí na poplach: podle nich to může obor vážně poškodit.

items.title: Ukrajina znovu dostává od USA informace o ruských raketách, řekl Zelenskyj
items.summary_raw: Spojené státy obnovily sdílení informací o ruských balistických raketách s Ukrajinou přes síť Starlink. Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj dříve tvrdil, že Washington Kyjevu před ruským útokem tajné informace neposkytl.

items.title: Další incident na letišti v Lipsku. Plot areálu prorazilo neznámé auto
items.summary_raw: Neznámé auto prorazilo plot kolem areálu letiště v Lipsku. Pátrání po vozidle stále probíhá. K bezpečnostnímu incidentu dochází dva měsíce poté, co byl na stejném letišti nalezen dron s bombou.

items.title: Recenze: Ještě švihlejší než dřív. Seriál s Dykovou je osvěžující podívaná
items.summary_raw: Třetí řada seriálu Případy mimořádné Marty pracuje se ztřeštěnou nadsázkou ještě víc. Dyková v roli neotesané, leč geniální policejní konzultantky nadále irituje okolí. Přitom jde zjevně o dílo natočené s láskou.

items.title: Čína ukázala roboty, se kterými chce bojovat proti terorismu
items.summary_raw: Další ukázka humanoidních robotů se pokouší představit i jejich možné využití v boji s teroristy. Aspoň tedy v pojetí Číňanů, kteří znovu chtějí světu ukázat, jak jsou v robotizaci na míle napřed před celým světem.

items.title: Fotky: Působí bezbranně, pro ochránce přírody ale znamenají záblesk naděje
items.summary_raw: Zelené mořské želvy se díky desetiletím ochrany dostaly z kategorie ohrožených druhů mezi málo dotčené. V Malajsii jejich návrat pomáhá zajistit ochrana hnízdišť, práce místních komunit i genetický výzkum.

items.title: Protivná novinařina? Díky za kompliment, pane ministře
items.summary_raw: Ministr Aleš Juchelka přišel s pozoruhodnou definicí žurnalistiky. Je protivná. Nejspíš ani neví, jak se trefil. A že nám tím složil poklonu.

items.title: Podle plánu měli zase propouštět stovky lidí a vyplácet vydatné odstupné. Místo toho ČD Cargo zase nabírá
items.summary_raw: Ještě před rokem ČD Cargo počítalo s tím, že bude dál propouštět zaměstnance po stovkách. Jen za rok 2025 odešlo asi 1400 lidí, především ve dvou velkých vlnách. A podobný počet měl podle tehdejších plánů odejít i letos. Nový šéf firmy Radim Ječný...

items.title: V zastupitelstvu seděl od roku 1986. Respektovaný komunista v Ostravě končí
items.summary_raw: Osmdesát let komunisté ovlivňovali dění na ostravské radnici. Polovinu této doby u toho byl zastupitel Josef Babka. Po komunálních volbách ale KSČM na magistrátu končí.

items.title: A new gas line or cash to electrify? California lets households choose.
items.summary_raw: When one of the nation’s biggest investor-owned utilities, Pacific Gas and Electric, wanted to replace Merrian Borgeson’s aging gas service line in Berkeley, California, she asked the company not to do it. Borgeson, who is the California policy director for climate and energy at the nonprofit Natural Resources Defense Council, explained that the repair wasn’t necessary: She was in the process of fully electrifying her home and would be replacing her stove — the only gas appliance left in the house — with an induction version during an upcoming kitchen remodel. At that point, she planned to request that the gas line be shut off. But PG&E told her it couldn’t wait. That week, the utility dug up her yard and swapped in a new pipe to send gas from the distribution main line to her home. Borgeson wasn’t charged for the service — at least not directly. The upgrade, which in PG&E’s service area typically costs $20,000 to $30,000, plus interest and operation and maintenance costs, gets paid for by all gas customers over the life of the infrastructure. A few years later, the new pipe sits unused in the ground. Courtesy of RMI “Now, I have no gas in my house,” Borgeson said. ​“But the customers all around me are paying for that pipeline for the next 50 years.” Soon, Californians will have the choice that Borgeson did not. items.title: Z Kolína bude evropský megahub, plánuje Toyota. Vidí v něm stroj na elektromobily
items.summary_raw: Toyota vidí Kolín jako strategickou bránu do Evropy. Japonská automobilka tam začne vyrábět první čistě elektrický model, nemusí zůstat u jediného. Náplň výroby kolínského závodu zásadně ovlivní změna evropských pravidel, která směřuje do finální fáze.

items.title: Ostrava má novou koalici pod vedením ANO. Motoristé dojeli na přehnané požadavky
items.summary_raw: ANO se na koalici dohodlo se Starosty pro Ostravu a hnutím Ostravak. Primátorem bude lídr ANO Richard Vereš. Z vedení města vypadli zástupci Spolu a Pirátů.

items.title: Data z Německa ukazují, jak se přiškrtilo Temu. Tržby klesly o třetinu
items.summary_raw: Čínská tržiště v Evropě ztrácejí sílu. V Německu jim po zavedení nového cla klesly tržby o více než třetinu a ve Francii se perou s úbytkem návštěvníků.

items.title: Hub může být několik milionů. Většinu druhů člověk nevidí, zůstávají pod zemí, říká vědec Větrovský
items.summary_raw: Jednotlivé kvasinky, žampion nebo třeba mnohatunová václavka. Houby představují svět velmi pestrých druhů, které se vzájemně ovlivňují v pro nás často těžce pozorovatelném prostředí. „Jsou to taková města, sítě různých organismů, které si dodávají to, co potřebují. A to se snažíme rozplést,“ přibližuje v Leonardu Plus odborník a herní vývojář Tomáš Větrovský.

items.title: Šlachta zvažuje odchod z klubu ANO. Rozčílily ho události na Znojemsku
items.summary_raw: Předsedu Přísahy Roberta Šlachtu rozzlobil spor kolem senátních voleb na Znojemsku. Neúspěšný kandidát jeho hnutí nabídl podporu kandidátovi ANO za 50 tisíc korun. Šlachta nyní zvažuje odchod ze senátorského klubu ANO.

items.title: Koalici v Ostravě utvoří vítězné ANO, Starostové pro Ostravu a Ostravak
items.summary_raw: O vedení Ostravy je rozhodnuto. ANO, Starostové pro Ostravu a hnutí Ostravak utvoří koalici. Primátorem se stane Richard Vereš z ANO. Původně se jednalo i s Motoristy, podle stran ale měli přehnané požadavky.

items.title: Byznys české rodiny, která se stará o hvězdy Hollywoodu, přebírá nová generace
items.summary_raw: Z recepce pražského hotelu vyrostl byznys, který dnes zajišťuje cestování hollywoodských hvězd i špičkových manažerů. Rodinná TYP Agency si vybudovala pověst díky diskrétnosti a postupně rozšířila své služby daleko za hranice filmových produkcí. items.title: The fire retardant in the seafood chain
items.summary_raw: In January 1966, a South African ship caught fire at sea. In port in Bristol, England, after firefighters pried open the smoking container, the conflagration spread and burned for five days. A little over a month later, a Liberian steamship caught fire near Rotterdam, ignited a storage area with barrels of petrol and sank. The month after that, a Danish ship caught fire off Long Beach, California, injuring three firefighters, killing a longshoreman and causing over a million dollars in estimated damages. The culprit in each fire was fishmeal, a dark yellow powder made by drying and pulverizing fish that, if left untreated, is known for spontaneously combusting as it decays and oxidizes. Tied to at least 90 ship and plant fires from the 1950s through the 1970s, fishmeal’s combustibility was a serious worry for seafarers, insurers and dock workers, according to a sweep of historical news coverage by The Outlaw Ocean Project , a news organization in Washington, D.C. In 1967 , American feed producer Cargill announced a solution: ethoxyquin. A crew abandons ship as the SS South America burns in Rotterdam in 1966.​ Sepia Times, NY Daily News, Evers, Joost / Anefo​ A fire retardant previously used to keep rubber tires from drying out and applied as a preservative on fruits and alfalfa, production of the antioxidant was soon ramped up. “Antioxidant treatment has made bulk handling an easy matter,” the director of the Canadian Department of Fisheries told an industry publication in…
authors: Ian Urbina, The Outlaw Ocean Project

items.title: Climate Change, Ecosystem Loss, and Emerging Infectious Diseases in Nigeria
items.source_name: Asian Journal of Research in Infectious Diseases
items.summary_raw: Climate change and ecosystem degradation can affect infectious-disease hazards, human exposure and the recognition of outbreaks, but the direction and strength of those influences differ among pathogens. Nigeria provides a pertinent setting because reservoir-associated infections, mosquito-borne diseases, waterborne outbreaks and climatically sensitive respiratory infections occur across contrasting ecological zones and unequal healthcare environments. This critical narrative review evaluates literature on climatic variability, land-use change, biodiversity, transmission ecology and disease surveillance, giving priority to Nigerian empirical work and using regional or global studies to clarify mechanisms rather than substitute for local evidence. The strongest environment-linked Nigerian analyses concern Lassa fever, whose geographical incidence correlates with climate, land use and socioeconomic factors, although retrospective prediction does not establish prospective forecast utility. Rodent field studies show that seasonal host abundance and viral detection do not necessarily move together. Dengue investigations identify under-recognised febrile illness and competent mosquito habitats, but antibody, vector and molecular results have different inferential meanings. Yellow fever patterns are inseparable from immunity and surveillance selection. For cholera, floods and climatic anomalies interact with water-system failures, displacement and sanitation disadvantage; direct…

items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in energy systems development: A comparative analysis of national strategies and future directions
Testing the backlash hypothesis in climate change messaging
items.summary_raw: Backlash against persuasive messaging can worsen polarization when two groups, such as supporters and opponents of a given policy, move their beliefs or attitudes in opposite directions in response to the same message. While recent evidence suggests that the prevalence of backlash may be overstated for most political issues, a notable number of backlash findings against climate change messaging in particular warrants additional investigation. This article details two studies that test hypotheses about backlash, as well as broader resistance to counter-attitudinal messaging, using a pre-post control group design that improves upon design weaknesses in previous backlash studies. Across two types of messaging about climate change, as well as a comparison issue, gene editing, I find consistent null results such that policy supporters and policy opponents are statistically indistinguishable in how they respond to the same message. Furthermore, whenever messages were successful in moving beliefs or attitudes, they did so in the intended direction. Using an improved analytical approach, the present research finds null results consistent with accumulating evidence that prior observed backlash may be the exception rather than the rule, even in the domain of climate change.

items.title: Hidden service climate archetypes in hotels: A text-analytic framework using employee narratives
items.source_name: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
items.summary_raw: This study investigates how hidden backstage organizational climates in hospitality settings shape latent service performance risks by leveraging digital employee voice data that are typically inaccessible through traditional survey methods. Drawing on 11,336 Glassdoor reviews from 378 hotels, we apply an integrative text-analytic framework combining structural topic modelling, sentiment analysis, and burnout lexicon matching to extract climate-related themes, emotional tone, and psychological strain embedded in employee narratives. These signals are integrated into a composite backstage failure index and used to identify distinct service climate archetypes. Importantly, the objective is not to assign individual hotels to fixed categories, but to uncover the latent structure through which hotels can be meaningfully grouped based on employee-generated narratives. The analysis reveals four empirically grounded archetypes—Burnout/Overload, Toxic Leadership, Career-Development, and Bureaucratic/Communication-Impaired Hotels—that differ systematically in their latent failure burden. By conceptualizing service climate as an emergent narrative regime rather than a purely perceptual survey construct, this study demonstrates how unsolicited employee-generated text can function as a diagnostic sensor of organizational climate. The findings extend hospitality climate research by offering a scalable, data-driven approach for identifying hidden internal risks and provide actionable…

items.title: Are Chinese scientists willing to engage with the public on genetically modified foods?
items.summary_raw: Drawing on survey data from 321 Chinese scientists, this study investigates their willingness to engage on a controversial topic, namely, genetically modified foods. Extending the Theory of Planned Behavior with topic-specific beliefs, we analyze how six key factors shape engagement intentions: attitudes toward public engagement, perceived institutional and peer climates, perceived self-efficacy, scientists’ own attitude toward genetically modified foods, and their perception of public attitudes toward genetically modified foods. Results of partial least squares structural equation modeling reveal that attitude toward public engagement and perceived self-efficacy are the strongest predictors, while subjective norms play a limited role. Crucially, scientists’ own favorable attitudes toward genetically modified foods exert an indirect, positive effect on their engagement intentions. We further examine disciplinary differences in public engagement beliefs and find that agricultural and biological scientists hold significantly more positive attitudes toward engaging the public on genetically modified foods than scientists in other disciplines.

items.title: Unveiling the intersections of domestic and transport energy poverty: An open data-based methodological framework for an integrated assessment
items.summary_raw: As cities become increasingly complex and unequal, limited mobility and inadequate domestic energy conditions are emerging as critical barriers to social inclusion. This study proposes a novel analytical framework for assessing transport poverty and its spatial intersection with energy vulnerability, contributing to a more integrated understanding of urban deprivation. A novel multidimensional and GIS-based procedure is developed, which operationalises transport poverty across five key dimensions—availability, accessibility, affordability, temporal constraints, and external conditions—and integrates these with established measures of energy poverty. By combining heterogeneous open data sources within a unified spatial framework, the methodology enables the identification of areas where transport and energy vulnerabilities overlap, as well as mismatches between their spatial patterns. The approach is applied to evaluate the vulnerabilities in the city of Madrid as an empirical demonstration of its implementation, illustrating how the framework can be used to map and classify vulnerable urban areas. The results highlight the potential of the proposed methodology as a scalable and reproducible tool for urban analysis and planning, supporting more targeted and coordinated policy interventions aimed at reducing energy poverty, transport poverty, and broader forms of urban inequality.

items.summary_raw: 1. New England (and Maryland) – The Trump administration is still messing with offshore wind farms, even while trying to pass a permitting reform deal. Examining the court filings reveals why they may feel empowered to do it — and I’m not sure how this ends. Last Friday, in a legal case brought by anti-wind activists, the Justice Department submitted a motion in federal court to send the construction and operations plan for Orsted’s Revolution Wind project in New England back to the Interior Department for more analysis. On Wednesday, the DOJ entered a similar motion in another case challenging the construction and operations plan for U.S. Wind’s MarWin project off the coast of Maryland in a lawsuit brought by the state’s coastal community of Ocean City. Trump’s actions led some to question whether the president was sabotaging the deal, and others to claim the media coverage itself was an attempt to kill it. Going further, supporters of the bipartisan bill claimed the DOJ's motions were precisely why the bill should become law, implying it would guard offshore wind farms against this sort of maneuver. items.title: Climate Races to Watch This November
items.summary_raw: No matter how well Democrats do in the House and Senate in November, it’s unlikely to mean anything new on climate policy in Washington, D.C., for as long as Donald Trump remains in the White House. That is not true when it comes to the other elections this year. Several states are on the verge of a possible Democratic trifecta, meaning unified control of both chambers of the state legislature and the governor’s mansion. It’s a position that could enable such states to either top off existing climate and energy policies passed in the last decade or to make the first real run at climate legislation in recent history. There are also several races for control of public utilities commissions — and, in turn, for influence over rates and the potential adoption or expansion of clean energy — that are being closely watched. Here are some of the biggest climate races beyond the House and Senate. The Re-fectas Minnesota passed its comprehensive climate legislation in 2023 after Governor Tim Walz won reelection in 2022 and the state Senate flipped to Democratic control. The bill included a 100% clean energy goal for 2040. Almost a year after Walz signed his bill, Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer signed her own , with a 100% clean energy target for 2040, along with energy efficiency and permitting streamlining. items.title: The Developer that Builds Local Support with ‘Right-sized’ Data Centers
items.summary_raw: This week’s conversation is with Harmol Samra, CEO of data center developer Host Digital. I asked Samra for a conversation because his team expressed a willingness to offer candid views on the industry’s problems with social license to operate — namely, why is the industry botching this so badly? From his point of view, many could learn a lot from industrial revolutions of the past, and they should be careful not to let mega-project expansions get in the way of broader acceptance of the data center sector. The following conversation was lightly edited for clarity. Can you start with your experience right now trying to get permission to build and operate data centers in the U.S.? What we do is we focus on data centers between 20 megawatts and 100 megawatts — we call them “right-sized” — that are currently energized and delivering in the next 10 to 14 months. So really focusing on the front end of that curve. To your question of social license, we’re focused on building the right-sized data centers that communities are used to seeing and have been seeing for the last 20 years. Very similar to any other industrial warehouse you would see in your community in a business park or things like that. We’re not building multi-gigawatt campuses in a community that has 20,000 people and has an overarching, overbearing impact. Global origins of tuna and billfish fisheries reveal the transition from coastal access to oceanic exploitation
items.summary_raw: Ocean ecosystems have played a crucial role in people’s lives around the world for millennia. However, questions persist about when, why, and how people first began removing biomass from offshore habitats and established fisheries in distant, oceanic environments. We explore the antiquity and evolution of tuna (Thunnini) and billfish (Istiophoridae/Xiphiidae) fisheries, two groups of fishes that occur around the world, are economically significant, and are ecologically important open ocean apex predators. The earliest archaeological evidence of fishing for tuna occurs ~44,000 years ago and billfish at ~10,000 years ago, with early fisheries for some tuna species appearing around the world by 3,000 to 1,000 years ago. Most early fisheries are in areas where tunas and billfishes could be accessed relatively close to shore (e.g., submarine canyons) and/or where these fishes may come inshore seasonally or during warm ocean events. Early tuna and billfish fisheries were often linked to ceremony/ritual, alongside advances in maritime technologies. With few exceptions, sustained and intensive commercial exploitation of pelagic predators in offshore and oceanic habitats is a late development in the human past, occurring primarily during the last 200 y. Our findings document a long-term continuum of human interactions with global marine ecosystems spanning thousands of years, including significant differences between the timing and pathways by which people became dominant ecological…

Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth
items.summary_raw: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6–enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3–enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible fat-1 transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3–dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced Arg1 + immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q + and MHC-II + antigen-presenting TAM populations…

items.title: A conserved Hox9–10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt
items.summary_raw: The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although HoxA/D paralog groups (PGs) 9–13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that HoxA/D PG9–10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that Hox9–10 function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five HoxA/D PG9–10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP) reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven Hox9–10 paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for Hox9–10 function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior Hox9–10 genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early Hox9–10 requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning…

items.title: Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming
items.summary_raw: Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q (which we term “QPCs”), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to climate warming.

items.title: Quiescence to proliferation transition regulates asynchronous mitochondrial DNA replication dynamics
items.summary_raw: Each human cell contains hundreds to thousands of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copies, only a small fraction of which replicates independently of the cell cycle. An asynchronous replication of the leading and lagging strands has been proposed to represent a major replication mode in mitochondria, complicating the investigation of mechanisms that regulate mtDNA replication. Using single-DNA-molecule analysis that distinguishes the origins and timing of replication of each strand, we show that the mitochondrial DNA replication machinery responds to the transition from quiescence to proliferation by dynamically dissociating strand-specific replication rates and modulating the physiological requirements for factors involved in replication and transcription. During this response, the requirement for mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) in replication initiation increases, whereas that for primase-polymerase (PrimPol), which is thought to function in DNA repriming at DNA lesions, eventually decreases. Thus, precise quantification of mtDNA replication rates at the single-strand level reveals the temporally dynamic nature of the mtDNA replication machinery during the transition from quiescence to proliferation.

items.title: Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA degradosome
items.summary_raw: The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major Escherichia coli degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of lacZ reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.

items.title: A “knob-in-hole” gate in the antibody C H 1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse
items.summary_raw: Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m 2 of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the F ab –F c hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal Thomasclavelia ramosa that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 F ab ′, i.e., the hinge and a F ab of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (V L + C L , V H + C H 1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline–valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal C H 1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 F ab ′ complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a “recognition complex” and a subsequent “precatalytic complex,” in which F ab ′ binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a C H 1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, C H…

items.title: Physical origins of speed control in swimming fishes
items.summary_raw: The linear relationship between tail-beat frequency and swimming speed in fish, first described by Bainbridge in 1958, has since been confirmed in species as disparate as eels and tuna. Dimensional scaling has explained why linearity should emerge at high Reynolds numbers, but the frequency–speed relationship itself has remained empirical, with no physical framework describing its behavior across swimming regimes, and no account of what sets the two quantities that define it: the distance covered per tail beat and the frequency below which forward motion supposedly ceases. Here, we derive a relationship from a balance of fin thrust, generated by a leading-edge vortex, and drag due to the boundary layer on the body. This framework yields an explicit expression for speed in terms of midline kinematics and body morphology. This formulation shows that the maximum stride length is set by the undulatory wavelength and the tail-beat phase offset, rather than by the conventional scaling metric of body length, and that no minimum frequency is required for forward motion. The model reproduces kinematic measurements from freely swimming glass catfish, published simulations, and Bainbridge’s original data. Without recalibration, it predicts the results of independent simulations spanning wide variations in wavelength, phase offset, and morphology to within ten percent. Linear scaling is thus one asymptotic limit of a more general propulsive relationship linking morphology and body-wave…

items.title: Nitrogen deposition does not alter the temperate forest soil carbon pool: A 14-y experiment on varied nitrogen fertilization
items.summary_raw: Soil carbon (C) pools in nitrogen-limited temperate forests are critical to the global C cycle, but there are no long-term experiments examining soil C, with various nitrogen (N) forms. Here, a 14-y experiment (100 kg N ha −1 y −1 ), with added N simulating atmospheric deposition proportions (~70% inorganic, ~30% organic) did not affect soil C pools, whereas organic N (ON) and inorganic N (IN) individually significantly increased values by 2.7-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively. Although no treatment significantly affected soil pH, treatment effects on pH were negatively associated with soil C pools. In addition, treatments containing ON forms increased mineral-associated organic C fractions, indicating enhanced C stability vs. IN. These findings enhance our understanding of N deposition-soil C pool interactions.

items.title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca 2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
items.summary_raw: Calcium ion (Ca 2+ ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in Trypanosoma cruzi , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca 2+ transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca 2+ release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca 2+ uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca 2+ transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca 2+ transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

items.title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations
items.summary_raw: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban stakeholders—including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators—in more than 20 coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains of transformative change (nature–human relationships, economic transformation, governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies were common across cities—car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights—yet were pursued with different transformative aims…

items.title: Reconstructing actin dynamics of the leading edge from observational data
items.summary_raw: Mesenchymal cell migration starts with the protrusion of the cell’s leading edge, enabled by the branching growth of the actin network. Two crucial molecular players in protrusion are actin filaments and the Arp2/3 complex, the branching agent. Traditionally, protrusion models are intuited from several perturbative experiments. Recent multiplex microscopy imaging data promise to change this paradigm by providing measurements of naturally fluctuating densities of key proteins at the leading edge of unperturbed cells. We report an attempt to reconstruct the mechanistic protrusion model from such data. We analyze fluctuations of densities of actin filaments and Arp2/3 complex and cell edge velocity using phase space and regression analysis to reconstruct linearized dynamics of the coupled actin-Arp2/3-velocity system. We then build a nonlinear model of these dynamics based on previous knowledge of this system and parsimony. The resulting models recover the rates of reactions and mechanical and transport processes in the lamellipodium from a single nonperturbative experiment. The models posit that the dominant nonlinear term in the lamellipodial dynamics corresponds to the retrograde flow of the actin network in the cell frame. The models suggest that the protrusion is dominated by a damped oscillatory cycle resulting from a combination of positive feedback from the Arp2/3 complex to protrusion velocity and negative feedback from actin density to the velocity.

items.title: A transposon inserted into HELD1 repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication
items.summary_raw: Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 ( HELD1 ), corresponding to the tassels replace upper ears1 ( tru1 ) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the tru1 intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance tru1 transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of liguleless2 ( lg2 ), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 ( brd1 ) and GA2ox1 , these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that HELD1 experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte HELD1 allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate HELD1 is an…

items.title: A muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein regulates postnatal heart growth through mitonuclear ubiquinone–PPAR signaling
items.summary_raw: Increased mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic respiration in postnatal mammalian organs are essential for adaptation to extrauterine life, yet the functions of many tissue-enriched, developmentally regulated mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined. By integrating mitochondrial proteome annotations with mouse and human transcriptomic datasets, we identified Coenzyme Q10a (Coq10a), a striated muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein, as a regulator of postnatal cardiac growth. Coq10a, the mammalian homolog of the yeast ubiquinone-binding protein Coq10p, is highly induced in the heart after birth through thyroid hormone-, Nkx2.5-, and Tbx5-dependent regulation. To define its physiological function, we generated three independent Coq10a -deficient mouse models. Both global and cardiomyocyte-specific loss of Coq10a promoted postnatal cardiac hypertrophy without impairing basal cardiac function or mitochondrial respiration. Instead, Coq10a deficiency altered intracellular ubiquinone partitioning, resulting in increased ubiquinone accumulation in a microsomal membrane fraction. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of PPAR-associated metabolic gene sets and induction of established PPAR-responsive genes in Coq10a -deficient hearts. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARα and PPARγ, but not PPARδ, attenuated the hypertrophic phenotype. Molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and mutagenesis identified PPARα residues that contribute to differential responsiveness to…

items.title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions
items.summary_raw: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle–cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano–bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design…

items.title: AI can persuade people to take political actions
items.summary_raw: There is substantial concern about the ability of advanced AI to influence people’s behavior. A rapidly growing body of research has found that AI can produce large persuasive effects on people’s attitudes, but whether AI can persuade people to take consequential real-world actions has remained unclear. In two large preregistered experiments ( N = 17 , 950 responses from 14,779 people), we used conversational AI models to persuade participants on a range of attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including signing real petitions and donating money to charity. We found sizable AI persuasion effects on these behavioral outcomes (e.g. + 19.7 percentage points on petition signing). However, we observed no evidence of a correlation between AI persuasion effects on attitudes and effects on behavior. Moreover, we replicated prior findings that information provision drove effects on attitudes, but found no such evidence for our behavioral outcomes. In a test of eight behavioral persuasion strategies, the strategy focused on information provision produced the smallest behavioral effect, though differences among the eight were small. Taken together, these results suggest that previous findings relying on attitudinal outcomes may generalize poorly to behavior, and therefore risk substantially mischaracterizing the real-world behavioral impact of AI persuasion.

items.title: PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the Predictability–Computability–Stability framework
items.summary_raw: As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal…

items.title: S -adenosyl-L-homocysteine triggers an adaptive response that extends lifespan through the YBT1 ABC transporter
items.summary_raw: S -adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) is a fundamental methyl donor; however, the physiological role of its byproduct and competitive inhibitor, S -adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), remains unclear. Here, we show that transient reactive oxygen species (ROS) production triggered by SAH during the early logarithmic phase mimics partial SAH hydrolase inhibition, extending the yeast chronological lifespan (CLS) through a hormetic mechanism. This study reveals that the dual nature of ROS in aging is determined by the specific degree of SAH hydrolase activity. We identified the adenosine 5’-triphosphate-binding cassette (ABC) transporter Ybt1 as a key downstream effector of SAH. Ybt1 localizes to the vacuolar membrane and facilitates the sequestration of SAM from the cytosol into the vacuole. Notably, YBT1 overexpression extends CLS, mimicking SAH effects through an integrated pathway involving target of rapamycin complex 1 downregulation, autophagy, and adenosine 5’-monophosphate-activated protein kinase activation. Our findings establish that SAH acts as a metabolic signal coupling nutrient and energy availability to longevity via Ybt1, defining an adaptive/hormetic response for lifespan regulation in yeast.

items.title: Systemic collapse emergence from climate-induced perturbations in transportation networks
items.summary_raw: The interaction between human infrastructures and external events results in loss of functionality or even complete system disruption through a snowball effect of cascading failures. Their complex interplay challenges their prevention, affecting the human population that rely on their functionality. Understanding how these networks respond to external perturbations is crucial for predicting and mitigating the impacts of disruptive events. In particular, meteorological events, while not preventable, can have significant impacts on human infrastructure. Here, we propose a model coupling the dynamics of transportation systems to the dynamics of external events considered as fields, to capture at the same time the critical behavior of the former and the level of influence of the latter. The impact of rainfalls on real-world railway networks provides a compelling case study, showcasing local endemic and system-wide disruptions above a critical value of the rainfall strength. Remarkably, localized perturbations on the wider network reveals the local weaknesses of the global infrastructure, and we assess them in terms of system perturbability and corresponding societal risk. Our framework opens the door to the quantitative analysis of criticalities in essential human infrastructure imputable to vulnerabilities that are set to intensify due to climate change.

items.title: A promoter G-quadruplex recruits Hrb27C to regulate NEMO and immune defense against Lyme disease pathogens in the deer tick
items.summary_raw: Genomic DNA can adopt noncanonical secondary structures, such as G-quadruplexes (G4s), which serve as critical regulatory elements beyond the traditional double helix. Whether promoter G4s also participate in controlling innate immune signaling and host–pathogen interactions, however, remains unknown in arthropods. In this study, we identify a G4 structure within the promoter of the NEMO (NF-κB essential modulator) gene in the deer tick Ixodes scapularis . Using a combination of circular dichroism, isothermal difference spectra, and fluorescence-based assays, we demonstrate that this sequence forms a stable, parallel G4 topology in vitro and in vivo. Functional characterization via luciferase reporter assays reveals that this G4 scaffold is essential for proper NEMO transcriptional output. Importantly, disruption of the G4 structure significantly reduces NEMO expression and increases the burden of the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi . Genome-wide expression profiling further reveals that perturbation of the NEMO G4 produces transcriptional changes that overlap with those observed following NEMO silencing. These shared transcriptional responses are enriched for immune-associated genes and ribonucleoprotein-related pathways. We further identify the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein Hrb27C as a structural binding protein that specifically recognizes the NEMO G4 through its RNA recognition motif domains and facilitates NEMO expression. Collectively, our…

items.title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems
items.summary_raw: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity (resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high-dimensional fluid flows and a real-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input–output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges…

items.title: Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in Arabidopsis
items.summary_raw: It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using Arabidopsis thaliana , we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that U 34 thiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant’s interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

items.title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning
items.summary_raw: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

items.title: Poly(phenolic) deposition is a prerequisite to poly(aliphatic) deposition for functional potato suberin
items.summary_raw: Suberin deposition in specialized cells is a critical aspect of plant protection, providing both water retention and pathogen protection functions. Tissue specific suberization during plant development is mirrored by its wound induction in cells that do not normally suberize and provides a robust experimental system to investigate the process. Suberized cells are characterized by a cell wall–associated lignin-like poly(phenolic) domain, and an ester-linked poly(aliphatic) domain, with the latter often laid down in distinct lamellar bands between the cell wall and plasma membrane. Previous work provides evidence that poly(phenolic) deposition precedes, and is necessary for, poly(aliphatic) deposition. To test this further, we generated RNAi knockdown lines of three wound-induced peroxidase genes, PRX19, PRX55, and PRX105 , in potato ( Solanum tuberosum ), the tubers of which produce an abundance of suberin upon wounding. Peroxidases catalyze the oxidative free radical coupling of phenolic monomers to form the suberin poly(phenolic) domain. The wound-induced suberin of PRX19-RNAi tubers had severely reduced poly(phenolics), reduced poly(aliphatics), and no apparent lamella. Functionally, wound-induced PRX19-RNAi tubers were more permeable to water loss and susceptible to bacterial soft rot. Overall, our data support the hypothesis that poly(phenolic) domain assembly is a strict requirement for subsequent deposition of aliphatic lamella within wound-induced suberin.

items.title: The basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are not fractal
items.summary_raw: The energy landscape picture is a central tool to study many-body systems. In particular, the energy landscapes of glass-forming liquids, jammed packings, constraint satisfaction problems, or neural networks contain a plethora of minima corresponding to competing states. Due to their complexity, these landscapes resist analytical treatment and must be studied numerically. We focus on jammed soft spheres, a paradigmatic model of glasses and granulars, to expose the limitations of standard numerical methods in resolving the true structure of energy landscapes. We show that the C-language Variable-coefficients ordinary differential equation solver is the one with the best time-for-error trade-off for this problem, outperforming commonly used steepest-descent solvers by several orders of magnitude. Using this numerical approach, we provide unequivocal evidence that optimizers widely used in computational studies destroy all semblance of the true landscape geometry, even in moderately low dimensions. Employing a range of geometric indicators, both low- and high-dimensional, we show that earlier claims on the fractality of basins of attraction of minima originated from the use of inadequate mapping strategies. In reality, the basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are smooth structures with well-defined length scales, a result that likely extends to a much broader family of problems.

items.title: Should Climate Activists Keep Fighting Fossil Fuel Infrastructure?
items.summary_raw: No researcher has been more cited in lawsuits against fossil fuel infrastructure than Peter Erickson . As an affiliated researcher at the Stockholm Environment Institute, Peter studies how pipelines and other oil and gas supply expansions can increase global carbon emissions. His work has been critical to the activist fights against the Keystone XL pipeline, the Enbridge pipeline, and others. But in recent years, he’s taken a more nuanced approach to fossil fuel supply — in part because, as he has shown, it can enrich the oil and gas industry in a surprising but direct way. On this episode of Shift Key, Peter joins Rob to discuss why blocking fossil fuel supply can lower emissions, why it can counterintuitively transfer wealth from energy consumers to fossil fuel firms, and what it all might mean for the future of climate policy. Shift Key is hosted by Robinson Meyer, the founding executive editor of Heatmap News. Subscribe to “Shift Key” and find this episode on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , Amazon , YouTube , or wherever you get your podcasts. You can also add the show’s RSS feed to your podcast app to follow us directly. But what you are doing is engineering a massive shift of wealth to the existing fossil fuel industry. I know…

items.title: Long after the Maui fires, toxic metals linger in residents’ bodies
items.summary_raw: In August of 2023, a series of wildfires broke out across Maui, killing more than 100 people, destroying thousands of homes, and causing billions in damage. Noelani Ahia, who is Kanaka Maoli and co-founder of Maui Medic Healers Hui, helped mobilize nearly 600 volunteers in Lāhainā, including doctors, nurses, and therapists. Three years later, the housing and health crises remain acute. Maui Medic Healers Hui runs a free clinic, but Ahia wishes it had 10 more to address the community’s needs. “The fire may be out, but the catastrophe is not over by any stretch of the imagination,” she said. The devastation extended well beyond the lives lost and buildings destroyed. Research published last year by researchers with the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa’s Maui Wildfire Exposure Study, or MauiWES, found that more than 1 in 5 residents had reduced lung function. Now, new research from the same project has found elevated levels of toxic metals in the island’s residents months after the fires, with higher exposure associated with impaired lung function. The findings offer further evidence that the health consequences of catastrophic wildfires can persist long after the flames are extinguished and the smoke clears. “What we consider and sometimes look at as a one-time event isn’t really one-time anymore,” Alika Maunakea, who is Kanaka Maoli and co-director of MauiWES, told Grist. Researchers don’t yet know how much of the contamination came from the fires and how much was already…

items.title: Advice from a climate therapist: Touch grass. (No, really.)
items.summary_raw: In my years as a psychotherapist, I’ve worked with many people facing similar struggles. One such pattern is embodied by a client I’ll call Emma (whose real name and identifying details I’ve changed for privacy purposes). She came to see me because, despite pursuing a climate career aligned with her values, practicing good self-care, and having a close community of friends, she couldn’t shake a persistent feeling of being “low.” She didn’t know what was missing. Emma was invited to an event at a scenic destination — let’s say, for your mind’s eye, that it was a wedding in Alta Lakes, high in Colorado’s San Juan Mountains. Imagine a scene something like this: The cool scent of spruce and fir drifted through the open windows, along with the thin, mineral clarity of mountain air. Now and then two owls traded low hoots through the dark, and something slapped in the water out on the lake. Emma lay listening for a long time. For reasons she couldn’t name, tears began to slide down her face, and soon she was sobbing. She wasn’t sad or upset. She described a welling up of joy, a sort of homecoming moment — a deep remembering that felt familiar yet beyond the reach of words. It was, she said, like “drinking clear, cool water when you didn’t know you were thirsty.” Ask a Climate Therapist tackles your questions about how to navigate the emotional side of climate change, with leading climate-aware therapist Leslie Davenport. Have a question? Ask it here ! Emma spent most of her workday…

items.title: Trump just effectively killed a popular solar energy program for rural America
items.summary_raw: Earlier this month, after a series of stops and starts, the U.S. Department of Agriculture announced changes to a long-running program that is supposed to help farmers and rural small businesses stand up renewable energy projects. The new rules , set to go into effect today, October 16, effectively make any solar power development ineligible for funding through the Rural Energy for America Program, or REAP. It’s the latest of multiple rollbacks by the second Trump administration that advocates say are essentially making the program unusable. Installing solar systems on farmland can cost tens of thousands of dollars upfront, which many agricultural producers may not have or may be reluctant to spend, given their low profit margins . REAP has long provided financial support to farmers to build out renewable energy systems on their land. These projects often provide multiple benefits to participants. First, they can help lower utility bills for agricultural producers and rural businesses by providing their operations with additional power. But farmers and business owners are also able to sell excess energy back to the grid. By cutting costs or padding revenue, these systems can be a lifeline at a time when farmers are facing escalating costs for things like fertilizer, fuel, labor, and seeds , making it difficult to make ends meet. items.title: Is coal really making a comeback?
items.summary_raw: Coal was on the way out. That’s how it looked last year, anyway, when the International Energy Agency forecast that global demand for the dirtiest fossil fuel had plateaued and was poised to start declining . But this year hasn’t gone as expected. The agency recently projected that coal consumption will climb to a record high of 8.94 billion metric tons in 2026. Headlines have declared that coal is “back in fashion ” and making a “ comeback .” So what changed? Blame it on the war in Iran, which choked off a chunk of the world’s oil and gas supply in the Strait of Hormuz and thrust the world into an energy crisis. Many countries turned to coal as a replacement. “The main thing is that coal is going up because gas is going down,” said Daan Walter, who leads strategy research on the future of energy for the think tank Ember. As for the idea that there’s a revival of coal, energy experts aren’t convinced. “I think it’s important to distinguish between a small short-term bump in coal use and a genuine resurgence of the coal industry,” said Christine Shearer, a coal analyst at Global Energy Monitor, which tracks coal plants and other energy projects. According to some experts, there’s a more convincing case that the crisis will accelerate the adoption of renewables and clean technology. Nearly every country around the world agreed to “ phase down ” coal at an international climate conference in Glasgow five years ago. Coal is the dirtiest source of electricity, releasing more…

items.title: Women’s Representation and Digital Paratexts in the Pirelli Calendar: A Framing Approach (1964–2024)
items.summary_raw: As digital environments diversify, brands increasingly construct their public image not only through what is shown but also through official materials that guide how those signs should be read. First published in 1964 for promotional purposes, the Pirelli Calendar has become an iconic case that makes visible aesthetic and ideological shifts in the representation of women within visual culture, while being continuously reframed through layers of digital paratext. This study examines the transformation of women’s representation in the Calendar between 1964 and 2024 by focusing on the relationship between visual codes—nudity, gaze/orientation, pose and agency, and Goffman-inspired indicators—and corporate digital paratexts, including official promotional statements, interview excerpts, and webpage descriptions. Using purposive sampling, three images were selected from each chosen edition, yielding a corpus of 30 visuals; six accessible official paratext texts were also included. The visuals were analyzed through visual content analysis and semiotic reading, whereas the paratexts were examined via a framing approach. Findings indicate that an erotic/objectifying frame dominated from 1964 through the 1990s, while, from the 2010s onward, “empowerment,” “authenticity,” and “diversity” emerged as central themes in official digital discourse. Yet certain patterns associated with the male gaze persist, and the relationship between corporate paratext and visual representation…

items.title: Integrating circular economy and policy synergies for cost-efficient lithium-ion battery supply chains
items.summary_raw: The accelerating growth of electric mobility has intensified the need for cleaner and more resource-efficient production systems within lithium-ion battery supply chains. Ensuring sustainability and cost efficiency in these systems is essential to reducing material waste, supply dependency, and environmental pressures across the value chain. This study examines how circular economy practices within the European Union, a region recognized for its leadership in policy innovation and battery manufacturing, shape the cost performance of lithium-ion battery systems. Drawing on longitudinal evidence that captures more than a decade of industrial and regulatory transformation, the analysis applies an integrated framework to explore the interactions among policy measures, technological capabilities, and logistics coordination. To empirically examine these relationships, the study employs a panel dataset covering the European lithium-ion battery supply chain from 2010 to 2023. The analysis combines panel ARDL and nonlinear ARDL (NARDL) models with Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to capture both dynamic effects and configurational pathways influencing cost efficiency in circular battery supply chains. The results show that cost efficiency emerges from the combined influence of recycling performance, government incentives, and coordinated reverse logistics rather than from any single intervention.
