items.title: The Invisible Drivers of Carbon Governance: NGO Network Mobilization and Policy Advocacy Strategies
items.summary_raw: This article develops a mechanism-based account of how nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) seek to convert network relationships into policy influence across climate-governance venues. It treats climate governance as the broad analytical domain and decarbonisation policy as one important subset. A structured review codes 24 peer-reviewed publications from the three most recent complete publication years available at the search cut-off, 2023–2025. The synthesis separates structural network properties, organizational capabilities, and relational qualities; records multiple advocacy mechanisms and policy outcomes; and distinguishes empirical evidence from contextual benchmarks. The reviewed publications most often discuss information and framing and coalition brokerage, but their codes overlap and do not estimate comparative effectiveness. Five China-focused publications provide scope-conditioned, theory-generating observations rather than a test of a general hierarchy effect. Only one core empirical study offers direct process evidence on implementation, and none estimates a comparable causal effect on compliance, investment, or emissions. Six propositions specify units, predictors, outcomes, moderators, and observations that would count against them. The article positions embedded network advocacy as an incremental contribution: its main addition is a conversion and feedback logic that links changing advocacy portfolios to policy stages, while recognizing risks of selective…

items.title: Smart Framing Through IoT Sensors
items.summary_raw: Currently, farmers assess their soil and crops by walking through the fields occasionally. This paper describes a more efficient method: small sensor units positioned in the soil which transmit data to the phone or computer all day. We describe the setup of this system including the soil moisture, soil temperature, soil pH, nutrient and weather sensors and the way that they are used to identify when to water and fertilize. We explain the system components, discuss the major sensors and wireless communications, and provide a simple testing plan. Previous field trials show that watering based on sensor data can save 20-50% of water without compromising yield and issues can be detected in minutes and not days. We also discuss difficulties (cost, limited network coverage, sensor degradation over time and security concerns), and how we might see things evolve in the future. Overall, sensor-monitoring is practical and can be used to reduce waste in farming.

items.summary_raw: У дослідженні уточнено співвідношення понять мовленнєвий вплив, персуазивність і прагматична страте- гія мовленнєвого впливу, що дало змогу запропонувати цілісну модель їхньої взаємодії. Прагматичну стратегію визначено як системно організовану сукупність мовленнєвих дій, прагматичних тактик і мовних засобів, підпо- рядкованих єдиному комунікативному або ідеологічному задуму та спрямованих на моделювання сприйняття адресата. На основі аналізу сучасного англомовного медійного матеріалу розроблено типологію п'яти провідних прагматичних стратегій мовленнєвого впливу: фреймування, солідаризації, делегітимізації, емотивації та авто- ритетизації. Виокремлення саме цих стратегій зумовлене їхньою здатністю охоплювати основні функціональні напрями мовленнєвого впливу: спосіб інтерпретації інформації; соціальну позицію адресата щодо неї; ставлення до альтернативного суб’єкта або позиції; афективний модус її сприйняття; ступінь її сприйманої достовір- ності та легітимності. Для кожної стратегії визначено характерні прагматичні тактики, мовні маркери та когнітивні механізми реалізації, а також проілюстровано їх функціонування на матеріалі сучасних англомовних публікацій суспільно-політичного, екологічного, кризового, аналітичного й науково-популярного медіадискурсу. Наукова новизна роботи полягає у запропонованій типології прагматичних стратегій мовленнєвого впливу, встановленні їхньої функціональної взаємодії та визначенні специфіки реалізації залежно від тематичного сег- мента…

items.title: Climate-risk narrative attention and carbon emissions: internal governance and coal efficiency as moderators, green innovation as a mitigating channel
items.summary_raw: Global decarbonization hinges on corporate behavior, yet principal–agent conflicts often undermine firms’ responses to climate change. Despite growing regulatory and stakeholder pressure, managers may prioritize short-term performance over long-term environmental goals when they perceive climate risks as distant or uncertain. Building on the growing literature on corporate climate risk, disclosure, carbon performance, and governance, this study applies a principal–agent lens to examine how climate-risk narrative attention (expressed climate-risk perception, Risk)—climate- and carbon-related language intensity in annual reports, not managers’ private beliefs—relates to firm-level carbon emissions (CO 2 e) among Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2024. We document a positive association: denser climate-related narrative attention is linked to higher CO 2 e under China’s institutional setting. A principal–agent reading can organize that pattern; we do not directly test short-termism or incentive horizons. We further show that stronger internal controls weaken this positive slope (moderation), and assigned province–industry coal productivity is associated with a flatter slope in coal-relevant industries, while green patenting is positively associated with Risk and negatively associated with CO 2 e in the same year—conditional correlations, not causal mediation. The perception–emission link is stronger among firms with low digital transformation, state-owned enterprises…

items.title: Overcoming Challenges in Carbon Credit Verification for Solar PV Projects in Nigeria: An ICT-Driven Approach
items.source_name: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
items.summary_raw: The feasibility of carbon credits for solar photovoltaic (PV) projects in Nigeria is faced with major setbacks, including data inaccuracy, high verification costs, limited transparency, and inadequate institutional capacity. These challenges affect project developers from adequately examining carbon markets and undermine the reliability of emissions reduction claims. This study analyzes an ICT-driven method to manage these barriers, emphasizing on the mobilization of digital monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems to suit the Nigerian context. By incorporating Internet of Things (IoT) devices, blockchain technology, and cloud-based platforms, the suggested solution improves data trustworthiness, decreases transaction fees, and impacts stakeholder trust. Case studies of already operating solar PV programs in Nigeria are assessed to find the feasibility and effect of such technological solutions. The study concluded that capitalizing on ICT can tremendously refine carbon credit verification processes, improve scalability of renewable energy (RE) projects, and allow wider inclusion in global carbon markets. Recommendations are suggested for policymakers, builders, and investors to aid the use of ICT tools for sustainable carbon finance in Nigeria’s energy sector.

items.title: Astrid Schomaker on biodiversity in a triple COP year
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02778-8 This year, all three major Rio Conventions — on biodiversity, climate and desertification — convene their respective Conference of the Parties (COP). In advance of the biodiversity COP17, Astrid Schomaker, the executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, discusses the irrefutable need to integrate biodiversity conservation into broader environmental action to ensure local and global security and prosperity in a rapidly changing world.

items.title: Renewable Energy Use in Small Rural Towns: A Case Study of Thulamela Local Municipality, South Africa
items.summary_raw: This manuscript explores the use of renewable energy (RE) in small towns to promote sustainable human settlements, using Thohoyandou as a case study. An exploratory research design underpinned the study. Using a combination of primary and secondary data collection methods, a randomised sample of 125 households in Thohoyandou town was selected, along with 15 purposively selected key informant interviewees. The gathered data were analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The findings showed that small rural towns, such as those typified by the study area, Thohoyandou, are facing energy access challenges. These range from frequent power outages (mean score 3.90) to frequent use of firewood (mean score 3.46) to low use of solar systems (mean score 2.46). The study recommended developing policies that prioritise the use of RE in small rural towns. Additionally, the strategic introduction of affordable, clean, and easily available alternative RE power to provide sustainable human settlements is recommended

items.title: Mō Tātou, Ā, Mō Kā Uri Ā Muri Ake Nei: Visioning Mokopuna Futures Through Climate Change Adaptation Strategies
items.summary_raw: In Murihiku Southland in Aotearoa New Zealand, Māori are already responding and adapting to the impacts of climate change. Drawing on twenty interviews with Māori leaders, environmental practitioners, and knowledge holders, this kaupapa Māori (Māori-led) study examines perspectives on adapting to climate disruption. Interviewees identified a range of whakapapa (ancestry)-based adaptation strategies rooted in intergenerational care, cultural continuity, and relational governance. Guided by Te Kahu Huruhuru o Kohikohi methodology (Kaiser et al., 2025) and Callon’s (1998) framing theory, the research analyses how participants contest deficit-based externalities of climate disruption, such as land dispossession, environmental degradation and reframe adaptation through four interconnected strands - whakapapa-based adaptive infrastructure, kaitiakitaka, ahi kā and utu; kotahitaka and strategic relationships; and visioning mokopuna futures. These responses transform externalities such as cultural erasure, land dispossession, and youth exclusion into overflows: creative, relational practices that exceed the boundaries of formal climate planning. Findings show that Murihiku whānau are restoring whenua, revitalising mahika kai, and embedding intergenerational knowledge in governance. Adaptation is framed not as a technical fix but as a relational obligation, enacted through kaitiakitaka, cultural resurgence, and mokopuna-centred planning. Participants emphasised the importance of…

items.title: Biodiversity and the Conferences of the Parties
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02792-w In a year containing summits from the three United Nations environmental frameworks, we consider how cooperation across the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) can facilitate implementation and impact. Co-timed with the start of the biodiversity COP, we highlight the reciprocal relationship between climate change and biodiversity.

items.title: Exit, voice, and adaptive livelihood diversification: Reframing coffee abandonment as transformative climate adaptation in East Africa
items.summary_raw: Climate change adaptation discourse has a habit of casting smallholder farmers as passive recipients of interventions designed to keep them producing for global market demand. This framing obscures both farmer agency and the power relations embedded in sustainability governance. Drawing on 385 semi-structured interviews with coffee farmers, cooperative leaders, and development officials in Tanzania and Ethiopia, we apply Hirschman (1970) exit-voice-loyalty framework to agricultural livelihoods, distinguishing exit from coffee from hedging within it. Exit, we demonstrate, is a reasonable response when voice proves futile and when broken institutional promises erode the relational foundations of loyalty. Our findings reveal farmers exercising agency by hedging within coffee through livestock, trade, and intercropped food crops, or by leaving it for khat, maize, and horticulture, in response to low prices, regulatory burdens, and climate variability. Critically, we document how external actors, particularly exporters and government officials, actively discourage exit, exposing how 'climate smart' framings often serve supply chain security rather than farmer wellbeing. By reframing coffee abandonment from developmental failure to transformative adaptation, we contribute to adaptation, political ecology, and environmental justice scholarship, and we ask whose interests sustainability interventions actually serve. Recognising exit as legitimate adaptation demands a rethinking of…

items.title: GREEN ENTREPRENEURSHIP FOR POVERTY ALLEVIATION IN CLIMATE-VULNERABLE AREA OF BORNO STATE
items.source_name: JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIAL SCIENCES
items.summary_raw: Borno State, Northeast Nigeria, faces a complex nexus of climate vulnerability, poverty, and insurgency that undermines livelihoods and resilience. This study explores the potential of green entrepreneurship as a complementary strategy for poverty alleviation and climate adaptation. Drawing on six focus group discussions with farmers, traders, and artisans, and ten key‑informant interviews with experts, data were thematically analysed using NVivo 12. Findings reveal strong community interest in ventures such as solar irrigation, climate‑smart agriculture, waste recycling, and energy‑efficient technologies, but progress is constrained by finance gaps, inadequate technical skills, weak infrastructure, and fragmented policy. The study proposes a four‑pillar framework (finance, capacity, policy, and markets) that integrates community aspirations with expert recommendations. This framework emphasizes blended finance, context‑specific training, coordinated policy support, and market development as mutually reinforcing strategies. Green entrepreneurship, therefore, should be treated not as a stand‑alone solution but as part of a broader resilience pathway in fragile, climate‑vulnerable settings.

items.title: Climate choices and attention are shaped more by politics than weather
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02775-x Climate change will further increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. Subjective experience and attribution of extreme weather events to climate change, rather than objective exposure alone, are associated with greater climate-relevant attention and choices. Political affiliation influences attention and behaviour irrespective of subjective attribution and objective exposure.

items.title: The PROMES Regional Climate Model: Three Decades of Development and Contributions to Regional Climate Ensemble Research
items.summary_raw: Regional climate models (RCMs) have become established as essential dynamical downscaling tools, providing physically consistent, high-resolution climate information where global climate models (GCMs) are unable to resolve. Added value is obtained over heterogeneous vegetation, coastal, urban or orographically complex zones. Temperature, precipitation or wind benefit whenever fine-scale processes govern the climate signal, as with extreme events. CORDEX initiative (since 2009) has further consolidated RCM research with coordinated multi-model ensembles covering all continental regions, enabling systematic uncertainty quantification of regional climate projections. PROMES RCM has been an active scientific contributor across three decades to the modelling community ensemble, with operations discontinued around 2015. This retrospective narrative review synthesizes and documents PROMES’s development, performance across Europe, West Africa and South America, and assesses its scientific contributions. This includes climate change projection features, extreme events (droughts, heat waves, or Mediterranean tropical-like cyclones) or land surface–atmosphere studies. Its behaviour within the more relevant international multi-model ensembles (from PRUDENCE to EuroCORDEX), with structurally independent characteristics, represents a scientific asset for uncertainty characterization beyond the model’s individual results, offering a legacy argument for preserving RCM diversity in ensemble…

items.title: ПРЕЦЕДЕНТНІ ФЕНОМЕНИ ЯК КОГНІТИВНІ МЕХАНІЗМИ ФРЕЙМУВАННЯ В АНГЛОМОВНОМУ МЕДІАДИСКУРСІ
items.summary_raw: У статті здійснено лінгвокогнітивний аналіз прецедентних феноменів у сучасному англомовному медіадис- курсі. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням ролі медіакомунікації у формуванні суспільних уявлень та інтерпретацій соціальної реальності, а також необхідністю комплексного вивчення мовних механізмів когні- тивного впливу на адресата. Особливу увагу приділено аналізу прецедентних феноменів як культурно зумовлених мовних одиниць, що апелюють до колективної пам’яті мовної спільноти та спільного фонового знання. Метою дослідження є виявлення когнітивних механізмів актуалізації прецедентних феноменів у сучасному англомовному медіадискурсі та з’ясування їх ролі у процесах фреймування, оцінювання й інтерпретації соціаль- ної реальності. Методологічну основу роботи становить лінгвокогнітивний підхід, у межах якого мова розгля- дається як інструмент концептуалізації знань та формування інтерпретаційних моделей реальності. У дослі- дженні використано методи когнітивно-дискурсивного аналізу, контекстуальної інтерпретації та елементи якісного корпусного аналізу. Матеріалом дослідження слугували тексти сучасних англомовних засобів масової інформації, зокрема аналі- тичні та інформаційні статті провідних міжнародних онлайн-видань. Результати дослідження засвідчують, що прецедентні феномени виконують функцію когнітивних тригерів, які активують культурну пам’ять та сприяють формуванню інтерпретаційних рамок медіаповідомлень. Встановлено, що прецедентні імена, висло- ви, тексти та…

items.title: Norm competition in evolving norm clusters: the case of humanitarian arms control
items.source_name: Journal of International Relations and Development
items.summary_raw: Abstract Situated within the research on norm complexity, this article studies norm competition during the evolution of norm clusters. It draws on insights from media and communication research to theorize how competition for limited attentional resources—such as advocacy capacity, public awareness, and agenda space—can lead to the blocking or displacement of weaker norms by dominant ones, resulting in partial norm emergence. I apply this framework to the evolution of the humanitarian arms control cluster, focusing on the delayed emergence of the norm against cluster munitions. Through process tracing and content analysis of public and institutional discourses from 1945 to 1997, I demonstrate how this norm lost the competition for attention twice: first to incendiary weapons in the 1960s and 1970s, and then to anti-personnel landmines in the 1980s and 1990s. The analysis reveals that issue attractiveness, sequence, and framing dynamics played critical roles in determining which norms gained traction. By offering a relational perspective on norms, this study advances and complements our understanding of the evolution of norm clusters. The findings have practical implications for advocacy strategies, challenging the dominance of one-issue advocacy approaches.

items.title: Collaborative governance for household livelihood resilience under climate change: evidence from China and a government–community–household framework
items.summary_raw: Enhancing household livelihood resilience under climate change requires attention not only to household assets and coping strategies, but also to the governance arrangements through which support, coordination, and feedback are organized. However, the mechanisms through which governments, communities, and households interact to shape livelihood resilience remain insufficiently integrated in existing frameworks. This study adopts a scoping review and framework-synthesis design to examine China-focused empirical evidence on collaborative climate governance and rural livelihood resilience. Drawing on 80 retained seed studies and 41 citation-traced supporting studies, the review synthesizes how governmental support, community mediation, and household response interact across scales. The synthesis shows that collaborative governance shapes livelihood resilience through five interrelated dimensions: risk perception, buffer capacity, livelihood strategy adjustment, self-organization capacity, and learning capacity. At the same time, collaboration does not generate uniformly positive outcomes. Public support may coexist with dependence, coordination with mismatch, and collective organization with exclusion. Building on these findings, the paper develops an evidence-informed government–community–household framework that integrates enabling and constraining mechanisms, feedback processes, and boundary conditions within a single analytical structure. The framework provides a structured…

items.title: Conceptualizing One Health governance for leptospirosis control through a bivariate spatial analysis of risk factors in East Java province, Indonesia
items.summary_raw: Objective: Effective management requires a One Health strategy integrating epidemiological and environmental data to guide intersectoral coordination. This study aimed to analyze local spatial associations between leptospirosis and risk factors using the Bivariate Local Indicator of Spatial Association (BiLISA) and to develop a One Health Cooperation Map for targeted control.Methods: An ecological cross-sectional study was conducted across 38 regencies/cities in East Java using 2024 data. Variables included leptospirosis incidence, climate, flooding, agriculture, and socio-demographics. Global Moran’s I and BiLISA were used to identify spatial clusters. Significant clusters were mapped to construct a governance framework assigning intervention responsibilities to relevant non-health sectors.Results: Global spatial autocorrelation was weak, but BiLISA revealed significant local heterogeneity. The analysis distinguished "hotspots" (High-Low) from critical "silent risk" areas (Low-High)-regions where low reported cases coexist with high environmental vulnerability (e.g., Sidoarjo, Lamongan). Nineteen priority regencies were identified. These findings were translated into a One Health Governance Map, explicitly linking specific spatial risks to mandated actions for agencies such as Public Works and Housing.Conclusion: Leptospirosis in East Java exhibits distinct local clustering driven by specific determinants. By translating statistical evidence into a practical governance…

items.title: Cross-Media Repertoires, Communication Efficacy, and Environmental Voice in Latin America: A Two-Study Analysis
items.summary_raw: Citizens encounter climate and science information through journalistic, digital, and interpersonal channels, yet evidence on how these combinations relate to engagement in Latin America remains limited. Study 1 analyzes 19,214 Latinobarómetro interviews in 17 countries. Weighted latent class analysis (LCA) identified five climate-information repertoires. Broader repertoires were associated with greater communication efficacy, but this H1 pattern was substantially attenuated after adjustment for environmental values. Efficacy related more strongly to environmental voice—public-facing action intended to influence others or institutions—than to private household practice (classification-corrected interaction OR = 1.094, p = 0.002). Digital-social and omni-channel profiles formed a high-voice tier. Study 2 uses 5948 Trust in Science and Science-Related Populism (TISP) respondents in 10 countries. BIC selected four science-information repertoires; five-fold prediction offered only weak additional support. Omni-channel respondents reported more science discussion, protest, and climate-scientist trust than low-intensity respondents, whereas policy-support differences were not robust. Overlap-removal analyses preserved both studies’ central results. Cross-country diagnostics favored common loadings but not thresholds, and common-profile LCAs were parsimonious despite national heterogeneity. These cross-sectional results associate cross-channel complementarity with communicative…

items.title: Methodologies and tools to support climate change mitigation and adaptation actions
Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
items.summary_raw: Abstract Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample ( N = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted.

items.title: Optimization of Renewable Energy Systems Using Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria: A Focus on Generation and Distribution
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.summary_raw: Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public-private partnerships, targeted capacity-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility…

items.title: Climate Change Impacts on Agriculture: Risks, Adaptation Pathways and Sustainable Solutions
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Climate change is an increasing source of risk for agricultural productivity, natural resources and rural livelihoods. Rising mean temperatures, shifts in the timing and intensity of rainfall, more frequent heat extremes, droughts, floods and changing pest and disease pressures can affect crop growth, livestock health, soil processes and farm income. These risks are especially important in rain-fed and smallholder farming systems, including many parts of India where production depends strongly on monsoon conditions. This paper reviews the principal pathways through which climate change affects agriculture and synthesises practical adaptation and sustainability options relevant to Indian agriculture, with attention to Maharashtra. A narrative review approach was used to examine authoritative assessment and technical sources, including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and a Maharashtra climate-change assessment. The synthesis indicates that no single intervention is sufficient: resilience requires locally appropriate crop and cultivar choices, improved soil health, efficient water management, diversified farming, weather-informed decisions, integrated pest management and supportive institutions. Measures should be selected according to agro-climatic conditions, farm resources and local evidence, while avoiding maladaptation such as…

items.title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration
items.summary_raw: Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the SOD1 G93A ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas…

items.title: Pollen tube integrity is critical for thermotolerance in tomato and is enhanced by loss of SlRALF1
items.summary_raw: Reproductive success of angiosperms depends on the ability of pollen to build a highly polarized cellular extension (the pollen tube) that delivers sperm to female gametes for fertilization. This process is highly temperature sensitive, but we lack information about how heat stress affects pollen function and the molecular pathways that impart thermotolerance. Here we show that maintaining cellular integrity during pollen tube germination and extension is the pollen performance parameter that distinguishes thermosensitive from thermotolerant tomato cultivars and that loss-of-function of one of four pollen-expressed Rapid Alkalinization Factor (RALF) signaling peptides can enhance thermotolerance. Moreover, we found that heat stress antagonizes RALF signaling required to maintain patterns of pectin distribution in the pollen tube cell wall to ensure integrity. These findings establish a molecular framework for understanding how pollen tube growth is modulated in response to the environment and show that RALF signaling can be altered to achieve thermotolerant pollen tube growth.

items.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
items.summary_raw: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion…

items.title: Distinct functional open states of the polymodal nociceptor TRPV1
items.summary_raw: The polymodal nociceptor TRPV1 integrates diverse physical and chemical stimuli, yet whether these inputs drive a common activated state remains unresolved. Here, we show that TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states that yield discrete single-channel conductance levels. These functional states appear to arise from distinct open-pore conformations, as evidenced by anomalous mole fraction effect measurements. Structurally, stimulus-specific changes in pore conformation were directly observed using site-directed fluorescence recordings, consistent with Rosetta-guided structural models. Notably, coactivation by two stimuli markedly slows channel opening rather than producing synergistic acceleration, suggesting potential conformational incompatibility across subunits. Together, these findings define TRPV1 gating as a stimulus-partitioned, multistate process and highlight opportunities for selective modulation of TRPV1 in pain management.

items.title: Changing contributions of emotion and reward information to learning through adolescence
items.summary_raw: From childhood to adulthood, individuals’ learning and decision-making may be differentially impacted by two salient value signals for adolescents: emotions and rewards. This study superimposed these information sources to assess their independent and joint influences on learning and choice processes. Participants ages 8 to 22 y completed a reinforcement learning task, in which monetary rewards conveyed information integral to making reward-maximizing choices, while emotional expressions conveyed information incidental to this goal. In some conditions, emotion and reward invoked congruent approach-avoid tendencies; following either information source promoted making reward-maximizing (“correct”) choices. In other conditions, emotion and reward invoked incongruent approach-avoid tendencies; following the emotion cue impeded reward capture. Participants completed several measures indexing the persistence of emotion and reward information on choice and evaluations of these signals. Statistical and computational models revealed that emotion-reward incongruence hampered early learning through an incidental emotion bias on value estimates. The emotion bias decayed as reward learning progressed in adolescents and adults but endured in children. Moreover, reward-based choice increased with age across the additional measures. Although participants of all ages were initially hindered by incidental emotion cues, adults’ shift toward prioritizing integral reward outcomes indicates that…

items.title: The impact of modulator therapy on the Pseudomonas aeruginosa cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome
items.summary_raw: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts P. aeruginosa physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that P. aeruginosa lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of P. aeruginosa transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate P. aeruginosa gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with…

items.title: Multivalent weak contacts shape chaperone–nascent protein interactions
items.summary_raw: Molecular chaperones interact with non-native proteins, playing crucial roles in preventing misfolding and in enabling efficient folding in the cellular environment. Trigger factor is a bacterial chaperone that binds to ribosomes, interacting with nascent polypeptides emerging from the ribosome and guiding their early folding steps. In contrast to the central role of the chaperone in promoting folding of newly synthesized proteins, its dynamic interactions with nascent chains emerging from the ribosome remain poorly understood. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence and optical tweezers approaches to directly observe and characterize trigger factor interactions with a ribosome-bound client protein at increasing chain lengths. We find that trigger factor dwell times on ribosome–nascent chain complexes increase non-monotonically with nascent chain length, and that binding to nascent proteins is best described by a combination of multiple weak, dynamic interactions that are established after the chaperone docks onto the ribosome and evolve during polypeptide elongation. Application of mechanical force perturbs trigger factor binding, supporting a multivalent interaction model. This binding mode may help to stabilize nascent proteins against misfolding while allowing them to dynamically sample conformational space in search of their native structures.

items.title: Retraction for Bonetti et al., Decoding the elite soccer player’s psychological profile
LEAP2 mediates long-term inhibition of orexigenic neurons of the hypothalamus in mice
items.summary_raw: Liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2 (LEAP2) acts via the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) to reduce food intake, yet the central mechanisms underlying its anorectic effects remain unclear. Here, we show that circulating LEAP2 accesses discrete brain regions, including the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARH), where it targets orexigenic AgRP/NPY neurons. Despite the negligible local expression in the hypothalamus, LEAP2 peptide is detectable in this brain region and in the cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting peripheral origin and central retention. Using fluorescent tracers, in vivo, ex vivo, and in vitro approaches indicate that LEAP2 exhibits prolonged binding to GHSR at the plasma membrane without promoting receptor internalization, thereby limiting subsequent ghrelin action. Using male mice, we found that central or systemic LEAP2 pretreatment results in a sustained inhibition of ghrelin-induced feeding that lasts for several hours after pretreatment. Notably, LEAP2 also suppresses food intake and c-Fos induction triggered by pharmacogenetic activation of AgRP neurons, indicating a broader inhibitory control over these circuits. Together, our findings establish that LEAP2 acts as a persistent inhibitor of hypothalamic orexigenic centers, providing a mechanistic framework for its long-lasting anorectic effects. These results highlight LEAP2 as a key regulator of energy balance and support its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity and metabolic…

items.title: Abiotic conversion of nitrate to ammonium enhances nitrogen use efficiency in paddy soils
items.summary_raw: Nitrogen (N) use efficiency is critical in ensuring food production while reducing nitrate (NO 3 − -N) to ammonium (NH 4 + -N) is widely recognized as a key for reducing N loss from paddy fields. Microbial involvement has long been regarded as the indispensable step for NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N in nature; it remains largely unknown whether abiotic processes can drive this. Here, using laser confocal fluorescence microscopy and thermodynamic laws, we find that Fe(II) ions in the rice rhizosphere exist on iron plaque in a specific manner with strong reducing capability. These specifically adsorbed Fe(II) ions (Fe(II) SA ) could mediate the abiotic reduction of NO 3 − -N to NH 4 + -N, accounting for 57% of the total NO 3 − -N reduction. When cultured in a sterile nutrient solution containing only 15 NO 3 − -N and Fe(II) ions, over 90% of N in the xylem of rice plants exists as 15 NH 4 + -N, directly proving the occurrence of NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N and taken up by rice. Theoretical calculations elucidate the Fe(II) SA -induced local electron depolarization enhances interfacial charge transfer which drives this reaction with the conversion of *NO to *NOH/*NHO identified as the rate-limiting step. We then propose a regulatory strategy to establish a stable Fe(II) SA /Fe(III) SA cycle utilizing FeC for controlled-release of Fe(II) ions. Two-year field experiments confirmed this strategy can increase rice yield by 16.1% while cutting half of the N input. Our work…

items.title: A GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis regulates VRAC activity by targeting LRRC8A
items.summary_raw: The mechanisms by which physiological signals gate the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis that directly controls VRAC activation by targeting the essential subunit LRRC8A. We found that the orphan G protein–coupled receptor GPRC5B binds LRRC8A and recruits the Src family kinase Fyn, which in turn suppresses hypotonicity-evoked VRAC activation. Disrupting Fyn binding to GPRC5B or substituting a predicted phosphorylation site on LRRC8A (Y362) abolishes this inhibition. Across primary astrocytes and reconstituted systems, GPRC5B prevents the intersubunit conformational rearrangements associated with VRAC opening without altering basal channel expression. In astrocytes, the MLC protein MLC1 partially sequesters GPRC5B, thereby reducing the GPRC5B–LRRC8A interaction, providing a mechanistic link to VRAC dysfunction in megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy. These results reveal a receptor-kinase-channel pathway that gates VRAC through Y362-dependent modulation of LRRC8A, establishing a molecular framework for VRAC regulation and its disruption in disease.

items.title: Estimating the threat of AI-agent responding across online survey platforms
items.summary_raw: Recent research and advances in LLMs have led to widespread concern that AI agents could pose as human online survey-takers. However, it remains unclear how prevalent AI agents are on survey research platforms and how to effectively detect AI agents. We validated a series of AI detection tests that effectively separated verified-human participants from both prompted commercial and purpose-built AI agents. Using these tests, we collected surveys on seven online platforms and find wide variation in rates of respondents failing AI tests, ranging from 6 to 41% across platforms (compared to a 2.4% false-positive rate for in-person human participants). We further demonstrate that undetected AI agents can impact the results of online surveys. Our findings suggest that while there is an urgent need for AI detection tests and consistent, systematic monitoring of data quality on online platforms, some platforms currently appear to provide data with a low rate of AI agents.

items.title: The historical domestication of a Clostridium botulinum strain used for the industrial production of botulinum neurotoxin
items.summary_raw: Laboratory production of botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) began more than 90 y ago for medical, military, and later pharmaceutical applications, creating one of the longest-running examples of microbial cultivation under sustained human control. A single Clostridium botulinum Group I lineage, Army Hall A (AHA), was established by the US military in 1942 and later gave rise to Hall A-hyper (HAH), the strain widely used for pharmaceutical BoNT production. We analyzed more than 1,000 C. botulinum genomes to identify AHA’s closest relatives and to infer the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) shared with its nearest lineage. Relative to this MRCA, AHA accumulated nearly 100 genetic changes, including 46 single-nucleotide substitutions, 44 small insertions or deletions, and several large deletions and structural variants that led to the loss of more than 80 genes. A nonsense mutation in mutS generated a hypermutator phenotype that accelerated mutation rates and increased genetic diversity. This event is inferred to have occurred early in the lineage’s domestication and appears to have facilitated laboratory-adaptive traits, including the lack of sporulation and increased BoNT yield. Competition experiments under standard growth conditions confirmed substantial laboratory adaptation, with AHA exhibiting a strong fitness advantage over a close relative. Together, these results reconstruct the genomic trajectory of a bacterium evolving under prolonged human-mediated selection and provide…

items.title: Interpersonal value regulates infection-risky social contact across 61 societies
items.summary_raw: Interpersonal contact is essential for cooperation and care, but it also provides a route for pathogen transmission between individuals. Hence, a key challenge for social organisms involves maintaining beneficial social contact while also limiting exposure to infection risks. Existing proposals suggest that this trade-off is guided by the interpersonal value of specific social targets. In addition, ecological and cultural factors, including historical pathogen prevalence, individualism-collectivism, tightness–looseness, and relational mobility, might also shape how people avoid pathogens. To test whether and how infection-risky social contact varies with individual-level interpersonal value and these societal-level factors, we collected data from 47,756 participants across 61 societies. Participants were randomly assigned to picture a social target - either a friend, acquaintance, stranger, or enemy. They then rated their comfort with infection-risky contact with that target (e.g., drinking from the same water bottle) and whether they would touch the target when greeting them. In all societies, participants were more comfortable with infection-risky contact and more likely to engage in physical contact during greetings with targets of higher interpersonal value. Such associations varied only modestly across societies. Notably, the associations between infection-risky contact and societal-level factors depended on target interpersonal value and were concentrated among…

items.title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction
items.summary_raw: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain’s functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging…

items.title: Structure-based targeting of Atg8 uncovers its essential role in autophagy-mediated detoxification
items.summary_raw: Autophagy degrades and recycles intracellular material, allowing cells to maintain homeostasis and adapt to environmental stress. In the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae , the core autophagy protein MoAtg8 is required for autophagosome formation and host infection. Here, we determined the crystal structure of MoAtg8 and used it for structure-guided virtual screening of a focused compound library enriched for natural products and autophagy-related molecules. This screen identified nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA), a naturally occurring lignan, as a MoAtg8-binding compound. NDGA suppressed conidial germination and appressorium formation, disrupted membrane integrity, and reduced pathogenicity in M. oryzae , with no detectable phytotoxicity to rice under the conditions tested. Mechanistically, the 5-lipoxygenase Mo5Lox, a target of NDGA, bound NDGA with lower affinity than MoAtg8. MoAtg8 associated with NDGA through Gln81 and promoted its autophagy-dependent delivery to vacuoles, thereby reducing compound availability to toxicity-associated targets. Disruption of autophagy or mutation of Gln81 in MoAtg8 increased fungal sensitivity to NDGA. These findings identify an autophagy-mediated detoxification route for an exogenous antifungal compound and reveal how MoAtg8-dependent trafficking modulates NDGA efficacy in a plant-pathogenic fungus.

items.title: Suspected distortion of citations in high-impact cancer journals
items.summary_raw: Research and scholarship are shaped by article citations, which underpin the communication of ideas, assignment of credit, journal impact factors, and author career progression. Given their key influence on author and journal metrics, citations can be intentionally manipulated to inflate the reputation of journals and researchers. Paper mills, unethical organizations that produce and sell manuscripts and publishing services, may also be manipulating citations, but the extent of this manipulation is unknown. Here, we show that molecular cancer articles sharing features with retracted papers from paper mills display citation patterns that suggest systematic inflation. These articles were published in journals in the top decile of journal rankings. Suspected paper mill articles received 50 to 100% more citations than other papers 1 to 3 y after publication, while paradoxically attracting fewer readers and online accesses. Suspected paper mill articles also cited—and were cited by—other suspected paper mill articles, which frequently appeared in journals previously reported as paper mill targets. Citations from suspected paper mill articles measurably inflated journal citation metrics. These findings suggest that paper mills inflate the citation metrics of supported publications and affected journals at scale. This widespread manipulation of citation metrics may amplify unreliable findings, slowing scientific progress and spurring unreasonable citation benchmarks for research…

items.title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons
items.summary_raw: The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix. However, the cellular basis underlying subtype specification especially that of eSPNs, and mechanisms governing the complementary patterning remain unclear. Here, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with loss-of-function we reveal that eSPNs share more developmental similarities with iSPNs and the transcription factor Foxg1 promotes dSPN and iSPN fates but suppresses eSPN fate in ventral region of the lateral ganglionic eminence lineage. Deletion of Foxg1 in progenitors forces both dSPNs and iSPNs into an eSPN fate. While postmitotic Foxg1 deletion impairs patch/matrix identity and leads to SPN aggregation. We identify FOXG1-driven transcriptional programs and key transcription factors that specify each striatal SPN subtype and patch/matrix identity, and uncover FOXG1 directly regulated cell migration- and cell adhesion-related molecules that control SPN migration. Our findings provide insights into striatal development.

items.title: Environmental chemical mixtures reprogram mammary epithelial development to epigenetic states associated with breast cancer
items.summary_raw: Environmental exposures occur as complex mixtures, yet the mechanisms by which they alter human tissue development and generate cancer-relevant tissue states remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a physiologically relevant 3D human breast organoid high-content screening platform that relates exposure-induced developmental disruption to cancer-relevant cell states. Screening of structurally diverse environmental chemicals as single agents and mixtures reveals heterogeneous but reproducible developmental responses, indicating that distinct environmental chemicals perturb different aspects of mammary morphogenesis. Focusing on bisphenols, we show that a low-dose mixture (BPA, BPS, and BPF; 3BPX) disrupts organoid development and induces transcriptional programs characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial plasticity, and partial epithelial–mesenchymal transition, accompanied by widespread DNA methylation remodeling. A 3BPX exposure signature maps to ER+ luminal breast cancers and is preferentially enriched in invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), a subtype characterized by epithelial plasticity. The 3BPX-associated methylation signature is detectable in primary tumors and adjacent normal tissue and is enriched in ILC. Together, these findings show that environmentally relevant chemical mixtures induce heterogeneous developmental perturbations that converge on conserved transcriptional and epigenetic programs associated with epithelial plasticity and tissue…

items.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder
items.summary_raw: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD–TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory–association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain–behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABA A α5, providing…

items.title: Superconductivity in the high-pressure tetragonal phase of UTe 2
items.summary_raw: Electrical transport and magnetic measurements have been made on UTe 2 under pressure P up to ~16 GPa to determine the superconducting transition temperature T c vs. P phase diagram in the high-pressure tetragonal phase. Superconductivity emerges near ~5 GPa, coincident with the orthorhombic—tetragonal phase transition; in the tetragonal phase, T c reaches a maximum value of ~4 K at 6 GPa and then decreases with P and appears to vanish near 18 GPa. Tetragonal UTe 2 has a relatively small upper critical field H c2 (0) ≈ 1.2 T at 5.3 GPa, smaller than the Pauli paramagnetic limit, and is orbitally limited with a coherence length ξ tetra ≈ 16.5 nm. This small value of H c2 (0) favors more conventional superconductivity; in contrast, the large values of H c2 ( T ) for orthorhombic UTe 2 exceed the Pauli paramagnetic limit in all three crystallographic directions and have been attributed to unconventional superconductivity, widely believed to involve spin-triplet pairing. The temperature–pressure phase diagram of UTe 2 shows a striking dichotomy: a narrow, fragile, unconventional superconducting region in the orthorhombic phase vs. a broad, robust, and more conventional superconducting dome in the tetragonal phase. This dichotomy is consistent with the proposal that U-dimers, present (absent) in the orthorhombic (tetragonal) phase, may play a role in spin-triplet superconductivity of orthorhombic UTe 2 . In the tetragonal phase, the normal-state electrical resistivity ρ( T )…

items.title: Synthetic reconstitution of planar polarity initiation reveals principles of symmetry breaking across scales
items.summary_raw: Development often relies on molecular prepatterning over large tissue scales, and how these patterns emerge is an essential question. Planar cell polarity (PCP), manifested as asymmetric distribution of junctional proteins within individual cells and coordinated across entire tissues, is a key module controlling tissue morphogenesis and organization. How tissues break symmetry to initiate PCP remains unknown. By reconstituting polarity initiation ex vivo using engineered epithelial cells, we found that collective migration acts as the symmetry-breaking cue, inducing front–back enrichment of CELSR junctions and establishing aligned multicellular CELSR polarity. Individual cells directly interpret the migration cue and remain sensitive to it. Strikingly, CELSR polarity arises without reciprocal VANGL–FZD interactions, identifying CELSR as the driver for polarity initiation. These findings reveal that collective migration initiates and coordinates PCP across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales, demonstrating that morphogenetic events act as a trigger for spatial pattern emergence.

items.title: Microbial niche partitioning explains N 2 O distributions and cycling in marine oxygen minimum zones
items.summary_raw: Oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) are marine hotspots for cycling and emission of the powerful greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N 2 O). Steep redox gradients host diverse microbial communities that produce and consume N 2 O, generating a characteristic vertical distribution, with low concentrations in anoxic cores and supersaturated accumulation in surrounding oxyclines. Although the accumulation is commonly attributed to stronger O 2 inhibition of N 2 O consumption than production, this differential inhibition is not consistently observed, suggesting that interactions among nitrogen-cycling metabolisms may provide additional mechanisms. To evaluate the ecological controls on the N 2 O profile, we embed a trait-based ecosystem model into an eddy-resolving simulation of the Eastern Tropical South Pacific OMZ. In this framework, redox energetics, metabolite exchange, competition, and grazing structure microbial growth, setting emergent niches of microbial functional types, particularly aerobic ammonia oxidizers and diverse anaerobic denitrifiers that mediate N 2 O cycling. In the anoxic core, cross-feeding tightly couples denitrifiers that produce and consume N 2 O, maintaining low concentrations. As O 2 increases in the oxycline, competition with aerobic metabolisms and intensified grazing gradually exclude denitrifiers. However, because they draw on more abundant substrates, N 2 O-producing denitrifiers persist to higher O 2 than N 2 O consumers, reflecting the vulnerability of…

items.title: Drivers of the likelihood of evolutionary rescue in response to novel infectious diseases
items.summary_raw: The introduction of novel infectious diseases has caused significant declines in many species, and in some cases, local extinction. Simultaneously, hosts might adapt to these novel pathogens, allowing population recovery, an example of evolutionary rescue (ER). Novel infectious diseases differ from sudden, abiotic stressors in that disease only impacts a subset of individuals within the population and individuals might be affected for a finite period. Whether ER occurs in an infectious disease context, and how likely it is relative to abiotic stress, might depend on both host and pathogen characteristics such as the scale of transmission (e.g., local density-dependent transmission only or additional infection through an external reservoir), the degree of fatality or immunity, and the adaptive pathway in terms of whether adaptive alleles reduce mortality, reduce likelihood of infection, or enhance recovery. Here, we use a stochastic mathematical model of host-pathogen dynamics with evolution of a novel allele conferring disease robustness to quantify how population trajectories, including the probability of and time to ER, vary across adaptive pathways and disease characteristics. We find that ER is more likely to occur with dynamical disease transmission compared to a lasting stressor that affects the entire population, indicating that protecting a subset of the population from stress facilitates ER. Among cases with disease transmission, ER is generally more likely to occur…

items.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing of molecular excited-state dynamics with correlated photons
items.summary_raw: Squeezed photons, which provide a quantum-correlated light with reduced noise, have emerged as a powerful resource for sensing the structures of matter. Here, we study the pump–probe scheme using squeezed photons whose spectral correlation of amplitudes can be tailored. A microscopic theory reveals a highly time-energy-resolved signal that is not attainable by classical pump–probe scheme. The results show high selectivity of accessing the molecular correlation functions, e.g., suppression of ground-state bleaching signal, and can significantly enhance signal intensity that surpasses the bottleneck by entangled twin photons. An application to a monolayer semiconductor model reveals a real-time monitoring of valley excitons and their dynamics, i.e., conversion between dark and bright excitons. We further show the intermediate squeezing regime–not strong squeezing–where time-resolved spectroscopy is favorable. Our work offers a paradigm for studying nonequilibrium dynamics of matter, in photocatalysis and optoelectronics.

items.title: Restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks via hydroxyl-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for efficient nitrate electroreduction
items.summary_raw: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) is a promising strategy for nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency is largely limited by sluggish proton transfer kinetics and poor reaction selectivity. Herein, we rationally design a series of hydroxyl-functionalized copper phthalocyanine-based covalent organic frameworks (Cu-COF-nOH) to regulate interfacial proton transfer via restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks. The hydroxyl functional groups in Cu-COF-nOH enhance water adsorption and dissociation to enrich interfacial proton supply. Optimized hydroxyl loading further induces the formation of continuous hydrogen-bond chains, enabling oriented and accelerated proton shuttling toward Cu active centers instead of stochastic diffusion. Electrocatalytic tests in 0.5 M nitrate electrolyte show that the optimal Cu-COF-4OH catalyst achieves an ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 93.20% and an NH 3 yield rate of 65.84 mg·h −1 , along with excellent long-term stability, outperforming most state-of-the-art NO 3 RR electrocatalysts. Combined with in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we clearly clarify that hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen-bonding restructuring plays a critical role in boosting proton transfer kinetics and reaction selectivity. This work provides a versatile interface engineering strategy for efficient multiproton/electron-coupled electrocatalytic reactions, offering insights into the design of high-performance NO 3 RR catalysts.

items.title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
items.summary_raw: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately…

items.title: Practical management challenges of stratospheric aerosol injection
items.summary_raw: Abstract Growing interest in using stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) to reduce the impacts of global warming has been matched by growing concerns about the approach. While much has been written about the challenges of governing SAI research and deployment, there has been little discussion of the challenges posed by governance and operational activities during deployment. This paper illustrates practical management challenges using three U.S. agencies (EPA, NASA, and NOAA) as examples. Although SAI deployment is expected to be governed by international institutions, implementation will require actions by domestic agencies within participating nations. Those agencies, regardless of country, are likely to face comparable national-level challenges, including accountability, transparency, expertise, legal challenges, and political pressures. Scenarios and assessments for SAI deployment will also pose technical challenges. Rapid development and evaluation of scenarios and assessments will be needed to examine unexpected conditions or new technologies and inform effective response decisions during deployment. This paper briefly examines proposed SAI governance approaches, identifies key relevant characteristics of the three agencies, and presents insights into those agencies’ relevance to SAI management and some of the challenges posed in putting governance into practice, and draws additional insights from small-scale outdoor studies. items.title: A new report just busted another myth about heat pumps
items.summary_raw: You may have heard by now that heat pumps — which transfer warmth from outdoor air to an indoor space, instead of generating it like a furnace — don’t work when it gets really cold out. That’s incorrect , as models designed for frigid climes can keep you toasty even in the dead of winter. Don’t believe me? Look no further than the Nordic countries, which have fully committed to them despite the region’s not-exactly-balmy winters. OK, so heat pumps are more efficient than ever, which is why Americans seem to be warming up to the appliances . But surely, since they’re electric, switching to them en masse will push the grid to collapse? That’s also false . A new report from the energy thinktank RMI finds that thanks to “headroom” in the grid during the winter months, three-quarters of U.S. homes — some 109 million — could adopt the technology, no problem. That would significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions and slash electric bills by over 20 percent in some states. “A substantial number of homes can upgrade to heat pumps within the headroom today,” said Ryan Shea, a manager in the organization’s buildings team. “We’d be better utilizing the grid capacity that’s already there, that essentially spreads those costs across more kilowatt-hours, and everyone benefits with a lower electricity rate.” What is this headroom, exactly? items.title: Electricity Prices Technically Dropped in September. Don’t Get Too Excited.
items.summary_raw: The national average retail price of electricity has fallen year over year from 20 cents per kilowatt-hour in September 2025 to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in September of this year, or about 2%, according to the latest update to Heatmap and MIT’s Electricity Price Hub . Great news, right? Not really. While this is the first year-over-year decline in average prices since September 2023, it’s mostly due to California moving around its Climate Credit to the late summer months of August and September , historically among the highest-demand periods on the grid. The state previously delivered the credits in April and October. But while this is a nice thing for California ratepayers, it does less to tell us about nationwide electricity price trends. Excluding the credit, average prices would have been roughly flat, according to the MIT researchers. And even with the credit, bills are still rising year over year, at around $180 per month, up from $173 a year ago (though down from this year’s all-time high of $217 in July ). Forty-five states and Washington, D.C., have seen their average bills go up over the last year. The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ recently released inflation figures showed electricity prices rising 0.2% in September from August and 4.4% over the last year, while overall prices rose 0.6% and 3.7%, trends largely driven by increases in the price of gasoline . items.title: Brazil’s election could determine the fate of the Amazon
items.summary_raw: Brazilians filling out presidential ballots earlier this month saw three-term incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pitted against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Environmental observers saw something else: a referendum on the future of the Amazon rainforest. “We are very serious about the risks for the Amazon if Flávio wins the election, because he is a climate denier,” said Carlos Nobre, a climate scientist currently at the University of São Paulo’s Institute for Advanced Studies. “If this candidate is elected, certainly deforestation in the Amazon will increase. We are in a very serious situation.” Flávio Bolsonaro, son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, is campaigning on an agribusiness-friendly, deregulatory agenda . In the first round of voting, he finished 2.2 million votes ahead of Lula . With neither candidate securing the requisite 50 percent needed to be declared the winner outright, the two will head to a runoff on October 25. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, left, and Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in October 2026. Pablo Porciuncula / Mauro Pimentel / AFP vai Getty Images Taken at face value, Bolsonaro and Lula would appear to have similar rainforest policies. Lula promises net-zero deforestation by 2030; Bolsonaro promises zero illegal deforestation by 2029. Legal is the operative term. items.title: Magic: The Gathering draws a bad hand with El Niño
items.summary_raw: On a Saturday morning in September, the game shop Dice Dojo was packed. Players sat shoulder-to-shoulder at tables lining the far North Side Chicago shop with board games stacked from floor to ceiling and a giant yellow Pikachu on the wall. They were eagerly waiting to crack open boxes of the latest Magic: The Gathering trading cards and face off in a tournament. Noel Camilotas spent most of the day pacing past rows of packed tables and helping players decipher the rules of the hotly anticipated new set. When he was done for the day, he walked out of the store with two boxes of cards. Despite that haul, Camilotas had hoped for more. “Some of the products I requested are not going to be available for me anytime soon,” he said. “One of the other products is not going to be available for purchase at all.” Wizards of the Coast, a division of the toy giant Hasbro, announced in August that delivery of its new set of Magic cards would be delayed throughout North America. The company pointed to a drought-powered traffic jam at the Panama Canal through which nearly 6 percent of global maritime trade and about 40 percent of U.S. container traffic pass. The drought this year has been magnified by the El Niño climate pattern, which spikes air and surface water temperatures in parts of the Pacific Ocean and sets off extreme weather like floods and drought across the globe. items.title: Oil Economics Are Plaguing Trump’s Presidency
items.summary_raw: This is Heatmap Daily, an evening news digest written by our executive editor. Subscribe here. At this point, the real October surprise may be the lack of one — because little seems set to change in the U.S. energy economy between now and the midterm elections on November 3. Inflation certainly isn’t budging. Prices rose 3.7% over the past year, and 0.6% in September alone, according to today’s new government inflation report. That reading was hot — a tenth of a percent above what economists expected. Surging gasoline and especially diesel fuel prices were to blame. Gasoline prices rose 9.1% last month, which pushed up prices above the economy: Transportation services, a category that includes airfare and Uber rides, increased by 0.6%, while food prices rose by 0.6%. (Read my colleague Matthew Zeitlin on how rising diesel costs can jack up food prices .) Staggeringly, fuel oil prices rose 15.3% — an eye-popping reading for a report where figures are usually in the tenth of a percent. President Trump seems to be running out of time to repair the U.S. energy economy before Americans elect the last Congress of his presidency. His last-minute deal to free up 2.25 millions barrels of oil from Russia this month — with another 11 million or so to come afterward — seems unlikely to lower diesel prices, given that it represents only a few days of U.S. demand. (The deal has already succeeded in undermining Ukraine, however, and led six Republican senators to rebuke him this week.)…

items.title: Soil and Crop Management for Climate-Resilient Millet Production: Fertility, Water, Establishment and Cropping-System Strategies
items.source_name: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change
items.summary_raw: Millets are frequently described as climate-resilient cereals because several species maintain production under heat, intermittent drought and low-input conditions that constrain major cereals. That description is directionally correct but agronomically incomplete: resilience is strongly conditioned by soil fertility, rooting environment, rainfall timing, crop establishment, genotype, weed pressure and the way water and nutrients are co-managed. This critical narrative review evaluates soil and crop management strategies for sustaining and increasing millet production under changing climate conditions, with emphasis on pearl millet, finger millet and representative small millets in rainfed and semi-arid systems. Literature published from 2000 to 5 August 2026 was identified through AGRIS, PubMed, OpenAlex, OpenAIRE, DOAJ, Semantic Scholar and Google Scholar, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative institutional sources. Evidence was appraised for design quality, duration, environmental representativeness, resource-use measurements and transferability. Across the literature, the most defensible conclusion is that no single practice provides climate resilience across environments. Integrated nutrient management, site-specific fertiliser targeting, strategic microdosing, residue retention, moisture conservation, timely sowing, stress-adapted cultivars and diversified millet-legume systems can improve yield or resource-use efficiency, but benefits are highly…
