items.title: How the Godzilla El Niño Will Drench California
items.summary_raw: California has around 3,400 miles of shoreline, ranging from the wild, foggy beaches of the North Coast to the sunbather-studded sands of Orange and San Diego counties. That’s a whole lot of border to share with the Pacific Ocean, especially when the water is as hot and tempestuous a neighbor as it is right now. Just ask the city of Long Beach, which this weekend was on the receiving end of some Super El Niño mischief. Swells from the storm briefly dubbed Hurricane Rachel “ annihilated ” beachfront mansions and flooded city streets, causing pieces of the local boardwalk to “ shred away .” “It’s never happened like this before,” one resident of 64 years told the New York Post . But while things might look bad in California at the moment, they can still get much worse. One disaster modeler recently estimated the state could see as much as $3 billion in flooding and mudslide-related losses alone this winter — not to mention coastal erosion, king tides, and storm swell. Governor Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency at the end of September, while many cities, including San Diego, have declared their own local emergencies. El Niño will likely peak in December , meaning that towns and cities across the state have just a few remaining weeks to finalize projects, whether that means improving drainage in landslide-prone environments such as Rancho Palos Verdes or distributing NOAA weather radios in areas likely to lose power, as emergency managers are in Santa Cruz. The…

items.title: The honey bee stinger: An unusual pump with collapsible double pistons
items.summary_raw: Most stinging animals deliver venom by contracting muscles around a venom reservoir, but honey bees employ a fundamentally different strategy. The stingers of worker bees have the unique ability to autotomize, separating from the body, to continue to sting independently. Despite more than a century of anatomical descriptions, the mechanics of venom pumping have remained unresolved due to the challenges of observing them in action. We recorded high-speed videos of active, autotomized stingers, combined with micro computed tomography-based three-dimensional reconstruction to characterize the biomechanics of stinging in the honey bee Apis mellifera . We reveal that the stinger functions as a unique double-piston micro-pump. Two lancets, each possessing a deformable valve, slide in antiphase within a bulb chamber. These valves dynamically deform to alternately form a seal during the downstroke and collapse during the upstroke, enabling pressure generation for pumping while potentially minimizing backflow during refilling. The inverted tear-drop shape of the bulb facilitates refill even while pumping proceeds. We explored valve deformations and flow behavior by constructing a dynamically scaled physical model of the bulb chamber confirming key features of the pumping cycle and propose mechanisms for valve deformations. The double piston design adds significant design complexity but enables continuous venom delivery in a compact, autonomous unit. These findings provide deeper…

items.title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
items.summary_raw: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. To determine how elephant carcasses affect below- and aboveground biodiversity and ecosystem processes, we collected soil and plant samples from 40 carcass sites (pairing “on carcass” and “off carcass” samples) ranging from 8 d to 7.7 y postmortem. We found that elephant carcasses released enormous pools of nutrients into savanna soils, increasing ammonium by 31×, nitrate by 7×, and phosphorus by 3× on average. These extreme ammonium concentrations were negatively correlated with the biodiversity of bacteria and plants, which were both suppressed at elephant carcass sites. Despite these decreases in biodiversity, ecosystem processes were strongly elevated at elephant carcass sites, with soil microbial respiration elevated for 1 to 2 y and herbivore grazing >3× higher for 7+ y postmortem. These results demonstrate that elephant megacarcasses generate coldspots of biodiversity but hotspots of ecosystem processes, unveiling a cryptic ecological function of megaherbivores that is extreme in both magnitude and duration relative to carcasses of…

items.title: P-body-mediated RNA decay controls neural crest EMT
items.summary_raw: Neural crest cells, a multipotent vertebrate stem cell population, undergo a tightly regulated epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) to delaminate from the neural tube and initiate migration. Neural crest EMT is controlled by a transient pulse of Draxin , which acts as a molecular rheostat of canonical Wnt signaling, and is then rapidly downregulated by unknown mechanisms. To address this, here we use in vivo reporter assays and live RNA imaging to show that Draxin mRNA is rapidly degraded posttranscriptionally via its 3′ untranslated region. We found that Draxin transcripts are targeted to cytoplasmic processing bodies (P-bodies), which are membrane-less sites of RNA processing and decay. Disruption of P-bodies by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated depletion of the RNA helicase DDX6 prevented posttranscriptional downregulation of Draxin and impaired neural crest EMT in vivo. These findings parallel observations in human patients carrying DDX6 mutations, who exhibit defects in P-body assembly and craniofacial abnormalities associated with neural crest dysfunction. Together, our results identify P-bodies as regulators of Draxin mRNA decay and reveal a spatially organized mechanism of RNA turnover that controls neural crest EMT during vertebrate development.

items.title: Correction for Ran et al., Versatile Xenopus tropicalis model with targeted integration of human BRAF V600E
Laundering and evasion in response to antislavery policies in Brazil’s cattle sector
items.summary_raw: Modern slavery remains pervasive across many economic sectors. Progress toward eradicating it has been partially hindered by a lack of tested, comprehensive policy responses. Using data on millions of cattle transactions in Brazil, we evaluated how ranchers changed their selling behavior after being added to the “Dirty List,” a public registry that names and shames employers found to use modern slavery. Dirty Listed ranchers significantly reduced direct sales to slaughterhouses that signed sustainable supply chain commitments but evaded sanctions by laundering cattle through compliant intermediaries or selling to nonsignatory slaughterhouses. These responses weakened the financial cost of listing to ranchers, and likely allowed beef and leather linked to modern slave labor to enter international supply chains. Our findings highlight the limits of downstream enforcement and underscore the need to monitor upstream suppliers to ensure slavery-free supply chains.

items.title: Imaging and recording of synaptic zinc in the brain by covalent chemistry–based semisynthetic biosensors
items.summary_raw: Labile zinc ions (Zn 2+ ) are stored in glutamatergic vesicles at specific excitatory synapses in the central nervous system and released into synaptic clefts in an activity-dependent manner. However, the precise roles of synaptic Zn 2+ remain unclear due to a lack of tools capable of analyzing Zn 2+ with synapse-level spatial resolution in vivo. Here, we developed neuroreceptor-based semisynthetic biosensors that function as integrating dosimeters, recording synaptic Zn 2+ by covalent chemistry in the living mouse brain. Using a chemical knock-in strategy, we introduced activity-based Zn 2+ probes with distinct affinities into endogenous α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole-propionic acid or γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors. These in-brain-constructed Zn 2+ sensors enabled region-specific mapping of Zn 2+ in synaptic clefts in the living mouse brain. Imaging-based analyses revealed differences in apparent Zn 2+ levels at excitatory and inhibitory synapses across hippocampal regions during kainate-induced seizures, providing insights into the physiological and pathological functions of synaptic Zn 2+ .

items.title: Integrating cooperative breeding with reciprocity and culture extends Hamilton’s rule to humans
items.summary_raw: We study how kinship and reciprocity shape giving and child care support in societies with limited access to markets. Extending Hamilton’s rule to incorporate reciprocity, we test it using behavioral data from dictator games and surveys in remote matrilocal and patrilocal villages of northeast India (N = 406 parents of young children). We replicate with data from urban Manila neighborhoods (N = 301) and the Solomon Islands (N = 624). Consistent with predictions, transfers to recipients increase with genetic relatedness to the donor and even more with relatedness to the donor’s child—a hallmark of reciprocity anchored in shared genetic investment. Nonanonymous conditions amplify giving, especially to nonkin. Cultural norms shape cooperation, but do not trump genetic relatedness. These results underscore the role of affinal ties and reciprocal exchange in sustaining cooperation, and suggest a mechanism through which cooperative breeding could contribute to the emergence of generalized reciprocity and human sociality.

items.title: Double periodicity of the AnkyrinG-associated complex in the axon initial segment
items.summary_raw: The axon initial segment (AIS), situated within the first 20 to 60 µm of the axon, is essential for action potential generation and maintenance of axonal identity [M. N. Rasband, Nat. Rev. Neurosci. 11 , 552–562 (2010)]. Its structure relies on the beta (β)-IV-spectrin/AnkyrinG (AnkG) scaffold arranged periodically underneath the plasma membrane, harboring diverse membrane proteins [K. Xu, G. Zhong, X. Zhuang, Science 339 , 452–456 (2013); K. L. Hedstrom, Y. Ogawa, M. N. Rasband, J. Cell Biol. 183 , 635–640 (2008)]. Although a ~190-nm cytoskeletal periodic organization is well established, the precise stoichiometry and spatial arrangement of AIS proteins within the ~190-nm spatial period remain rudimentary, mostly for lack of sufficient spatial resolution and labeling efficiency. Here, using expansion microscopy and cryoelectron tomography, which overcome these technical limitations, we present data on the organization of the AnkG-associated complex within the ~190-nm spatial period. We demonstrate that exactly two AnkG molecules are situated within each period and with their C termini separated by ~80 nm. By contrast, the AnkG-associated cell-adhesion protein neurofascin-186 appears in clusters of varying sizes that are consistent with the periodic organization of AnkG pairs, yet suggesting a more complex molecular arrangement between the two molecules. Altogether, our approach provides insights into AIS molecular organization and protein stoichiometry.

items.title: Antiferromagnetism and tightly bound Cooper pairs induced by kinetic frustration
items.summary_raw: Antiferromagnetism and superconductivity are often viewed as competing orders in correlated electron systems. Here, we demonstrate that kinetic frustration in hole motion facilitates their coexistence within the square-lattice repulsive Hubbard model. Combining exact analytical solutions on tailored geometries with large-scale numerical simulations, we reveal a robust pairing mechanism: Holes on opposite sublattices behave as if they carry opposite effective charges due to spin singlet formation from kinetic frustration. This emergent property suppresses phase separation and fosters a coherent d -wave superconducting channel embedded within a long-range antiferromagnetic background. Our findings establish a minimal yet broadly applicable framework for stabilizing strong-coupling superconductivity in doped Mott insulators.

items.title: Domino-like propagation of localized deformation in origami structures
Interfacial microenvironments enable abiotic ribonucleoside formation in micro- and nanoscale compartments
items.summary_raw: The abiotic emergence of ribonucleosides remains a central challenge in origin-of-life research because ribonucleosides form inefficiently and are often unstable under prebiotically plausible conditions. Here we show that interfacial microenvironments within aqueous micro- and nanoscale compartments containing D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and nucleobases promote ribonucleoside formation by creating reaction-permissive physicochemical conditions independent of the specific compartment type. Across a diverse range of compartmentalized systems, including gas–oil–water micro/nanobubbles, gas–water micro/nanobubbles, microscale lipid-bilayer vesicles, and oil–water emulsion systems, ribonucleosides form abiotically in the absence of enzymatic catalysis. Under selected interfacial conditions, multiple ribonucleosides, including cytidine, are generated without added catalysts. Comparison among these systems reveals that interfacial architecture and coupled physicochemical properties strongly influence both reaction efficiency and product stability. CO 2 -based micro/nanobubbles support sustained cytidine accumulation, highlighting the importance of coupled gas–liquid and liquid–liquid interfaces. Ribonucleoside synthesis also depends on compartment size, whereas variations in oil content within micro/nanobubbles selectively modulate inosine formation, underscoring the sensitivity of nucleoside chemistry to interfacial properties. These findings identify interfacial microenvironments…

items.title: Correction for Blawas et al., Sprint-like cardiac dynamics support repeated acrobatic lunges in foraging rorqual whales
A Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex drives enhanced depotentiation in a mouse model of improved cognitive flexibility
items.summary_raw: Memory updating promotes cognitive flexibility by enabling suppression of outdated information to optimize behavioral strategies in response to a changing environment. While some circuits involved have been identified, the synaptic mechanisms underlying this process remain uncertain. Here, using a recently developed Kv4.2 knock-in mouse model (Kv4.2TA), we identify a metaplasticity in the hippocampus that accompanies an improvement in cognitive flexibility. Mutation of a C-terminal phosphorylation site (T607) in the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated K + channel protein Kv4.2 drives boosted depotentiation of spike timing-dependent long-term synaptic potentiation mediated by mGluR5 receptors, putative constituents of Kv4.2 macromolecular complexes. We found that mGluR5 receptors are required for the improved cognitive flexibility observed in Kv4.2TA mice. These findings reveal a synaptic correlate associated with memory updating in cognitive flexibility and spotlight the Kv4.2-mGluR5 complex as a therapeutic target for disorders characterized by impairments in cognitive flexibility.

items.title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication
items.summary_raw: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human…

items.title: Multidimensional vulnerabilities of informal settlements in the Urban South
items.summary_raw: Informal settlements are widespread and rapidly growing, often associated with high vulnerabilities. However, global-scale understanding on their spatial distribution and complexity of vulnerability is limited. Here, we delineate the informal settlements across a sample of 1,914 cities of the Global South by integrating Sentinel-2 imagery with deep learning models, and we explore the heterogeneity of vulnerability using Urban Informal Settlement Vulnerability Index that encompasses living conditions, social infrastructure, and environmental risk. We found that Urban Informal Settlements cover 12.94 ± 2.52% of their total urban areas (approximately 34.04 × 10 3 km 2 ), especially in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Middle Asia. Sub-Saharan African cities have the highest vulnerability of informal settlements, with 31.75 ± 6.20% of total urban areas being occupied by informal settlements, while East Asian cities exhibit relatively low vulnerability across all dimensions. We also find that urban informal settlements with high environmental exposure are widespread in the Global South, and there is a significantly polarized distribution between “low” and “high” vulnerability categories. The findings highlight the disparate distribution of multidimensional vulnerability in informal settlements across the Urban South, providing a comparative evidence base for further local assessment and context-specific policy discussions related to SDG 11.

items.title: Discovery and characterization of miranthins, “Trojan horse” antibiotic modulators of bacterial composition in the oral microbiome
items.summary_raw: Bacteria of the human microbiota encode an abundance of natural products that likely mediate bacterial competition, local colonization patterns, and human health and disease. However, very few of these compounds have been identified and characterized to date. During our investigation of Streptococcus mitis , an important early colonizer of the oral cavity, we identified and structurally characterized a family of peptide natural products, termed miranthins herein, that contain an unusual macrocycle formed by an Asp-Cys β-carbon thioether crosslink. We determined that the most abundantly secreted miranthin is a “Trojan horse” antibiotic that enters sensitive cells via the Ami oligopeptide transporter, is hydrolyzed and activated by aminopeptidase N, and subsequently inhibits ribosomal translation to curb the growth of streptococcal competitors. The miranthins are narrow-spectrum antibiotics that could enable S. mitis to modulate community dynamics in the oral cavity, highlighting the importance of peptide natural products in interspecies competition in the microbiome.

items.title: A water-pinning hot spot drives templated tau aggregation
items.summary_raw: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured solvation water has been proposed to be a signature of such hot spots at both the tau fibril-end surface and soluble tau monomers. Although jR2R3-P301L tau exhibits a heterogeneous hydration landscape in its intrinsically disordered state, with enhanced water structuring near the P301L mutation site, it is unclear whether a localized hotspot exists at the fibril end surface and surface water facilitates the initial contacts in templated aggregation. Using rapid 1 H- 15 N SOFAST-HMQC NMR to track seed-induced aggregation of jR2R3-P301L in real time, complemented by molecular dynamics simulation of fibril surface hydration, we identify a residue-specific pinning hotspot that is prone to dewetting followed by sequential folding and incorporation of the remaining segment in a two-step dock-and-lock process. Site-specific spin labeling further demonstrates that blocking this pinning hotspot disrupts…

items.title: Competing presynaptic protein assemblies coordinate basal neurotransmission with homeostatic plasticity
items.summary_raw: Neural circuits establish a stable basal level of synaptic transmission that is maintained throughout life. When synaptic activity is perturbed, homeostatic mechanisms restore this set point, but how neurons reconcile long-term stability and rapid compensatory plasticity remains unclear. Here, we identify two competing presynaptic multimolecular complexes that control steady-state transmission and homeostatic potentiation and define the molecular switch that enables transitions between these functional states. At Drosophila neuromuscular junction, the transmembrane protein PlexinB (PlexB) and the auxiliary subunit Neto-α regulate both basal synaptic function and homeostatic plasticity. PlexB association with presynaptic KaiR1D/Neto-α receptor complexes modulates channel properties and fine-tunes neurotransmitter release, whereas PlexB signaling with Semaphorin2b (Sema2b) and Neto-α drives homeostatic potentiation. KaiR1D and Sema2b/PlexB compete for a limited pool of presynaptic Neto-α. Motor neurons switch from steady-state transmission to homeostatic potentiation by exchanging KaiR1D/Neto-α/PlexB complexes for Neto-α/PlexB/Sema2b. Critically, Neto-α must dissociate from KaiR1D-containing complexes to initiate the homeostatic response. Variants of Neto-α or KaiR1D that fail to dissociate support normal basal neurotransmission but abolish homeostatic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that dynamic reorganization of competing presynaptic protein assemblies enables neurons…

items.title: Correction for Johnson et al., Antagonistic regulation of nitrogen and drought signaling mediated by NIN-like protein 7 transcription factor in Arabidopsis thaliana
Phylogenomics confirms Palaeoptera monophyly and illuminates the origin of winged insects
items.summary_raw: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies…

items.title: Cell identity competes with surface tension to determine stromal organization in tumor spheroids beyond the CAF shell paradigm
items.summary_raw: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are often found forming a peripheral stromal barrier around tumors. Here, this paradigm is challenged using microfabricated 3D cancer–CAF spheroid models combined with quantitative magnetic force tensiometry. A surface tension atlas is established for eight cancer cell lines, three CAF populations, and heterotypic tumor–CAF assemblies, spanning nearly two orders of magnitude. Surface tension is first shown to govern spheroid morphology and modulate drug response. Besides, CAFs consistently occupy the highest end of the surface tension hierarchy, predicting core rather than peripheral localization and directly challenging the shell paradigm. Yet confocal imaging reveals not only central accumulation but also complete CAF-tumor mixing, including in spheroids where cancer cells exhibit surface tensions nearly two orders of magnitude lower than CAFs. Surface tension alone therefore fails to predict CAF organization. Instead, the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) state of cancer cells emerges as a major determinant: epithelial-like tumors promote CAF core accumulation, whereas mesenchymal-like states favor persistent mixing. Peripheral CAF localization emerges only under restricted conditions combining high tumor cohesion and sequential stromal recruitment. Together, these results identify surface tension, EMT state, and assembly chronology as joint determinants of tumor–stroma architecture, revealing a context-dependent organization…

items.title: A multiscale framework for heme crystallization inhibition: From single-molecule step-capping to parasite suppression
items.summary_raw: Heme crystallization is central to malaria parasites’ survival during the erythrocytic stage of the disease, yet how clinically relevant antimalarial drugs modulate this process at the molecular level remains unclear. Here we employ stage-resolved parasite assays and multiscale in vitro approaches to explore the interactions between lumefantrine (LF), one of the popular components of current combination therapies, and hematin crystallization. Pulse LF suppresses Plasmodium falciparum during both ring and trophozoite stages. Under biomimetic conditions, LF markedly reduces β-hematin crystal growth rates. High-resolution atomic force microscopy reveals that individual LF molecules bind directly to crystal steps, physically constraining step motion through a previously unreported step-capping mechanism. This localized inhibition propagates to the mesoscale, producing step broadening, reduced interstep spacing, and causing surface kinetic roughening. In contrast to its strong inhibition of crystal growth, LF enhances hematin nucleation by promoting the formation of mesoscopic hematin-rich clusters, as detected by a combination of scattering and microscopy techniques. Attachment of the nucleated crystallites to larger crystal surfaces initiates a nonclassical inhibition sequence by straining the crystal interface, which further impedes step growth.

items.title: Taylor’s law beyond finite moments: A route to dynamic financial risk
Multiyear dual-isotope fingerprinting at South Asian receptor sites constrains carbon monoxide sources and enhanced oxidation
items.summary_raw: Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. Based on nine winter-long dual-isotope campaigns at two South Asian receptor sites intercepting the continental outflow, we quantified CO source contributions and emission–sink dynamics. Combustion accounts for 68 to 74% of South Asia regional CO (including 34 to 37% from biomass burning) with secondary atmospheric oxidation contributing 26 to 32% (dominated by oxidation of nonmethane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) at 21 to 26%, with methane oxidation contributing 5.5 to 6.4%). These isotope-observational constraints suggest a twice higher role for atmospheric oxidation than in model estimates. Spatially, the absolute contributions of both primary and secondary CO decrease from the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the northern Indian Ocean, while the relative contribution of oxidation-derived CO increases, indicating enhanced secondary CO production near source regions. Observation-model comparison suggests that transport from the continental areas dominates CO over adjacent oceanic regions, with minor local production. During the COVID-19 emission perturbation, combustion-derived CO fell sharply in absolute terms, NMVOC-derived CO rose, and CH 4 -derived CO remained stable, providing an observational constraint on the sensitivity of atmospheric oxidation to emission changes. Our results reveal a significant contribution of CO from atmospheric…

items.title: Thermodynamic origin of atmospheric new particle formation: Theory for stable nucleating pairs
items.summary_raw: Atmospheric new particle formation (NPF) has been observed across virtually all tropospheric environments, yet the meteorological conditions that favor or suppress it have resisted clear theoretical resolution. Here we show that, for neutral chemistries in which a strongly bound molecular pair constitutes the critical cluster, the thermodynamic precondition for NPF is set by a single quantity: the effective binding free energy of that pair, Δ G AB ° ( T , RH ) , which captures the competing influences of temperature and relative humidity in a closed-form analytical framework. Applied to the sulfuric acid–dimethylamine system in the boundary layer, the theory reproduces observed clustering across laboratory experiments and field campaigns spanning a polluted megacity, a remote high-altitude site, and an ultra-pristine boreal peatland, all without kinetic fitting parameters; precursor concentrations and the condensation sink enter as separable factors that govern the subsequent production rate. The framework reveals an optimal Δ G AB ° that maximizes cluster production, providing a thermodynamic basis for why NPF peaks at midday, favors spring over other seasons, occurs under heat wave conditions despite temperatures approaching + 40 ° C, and can even arise on rare evenings in near-pristine conditions. More broadly, the theory exposes the inherent relationship between atmospheric conditions and the earliest steps of particle formation, offering a general interpretive tool that…

items.title: Coordinated transformations of the labyrinth and occiput during the dinosaur–bird transition
items.summary_raw: Evolutionary shape changes of the vertebrate semicircular canals (SCCs) are often ascribed to evolutionary transitions in locomotion, including the origin of flight during the dinosaur–bird transition. However, the potential for transformations of braincase architecture to influence SCC shape independent of sensory-functional adaptation has generally been overlooked. We evaluate the influence of both factors using a large dataset of 146 living and recently extinct crown birds, including taxa representing ~24 independent evolutionary losses of flight, together with Mesozoic stem avialans, nonavialan dinosaurs, and pterosaurs. Among crown birds, evolutionary changes in locomotor capabilities, including the total loss of flight, have only weak effects on SCC shape, contrasting with large effects from changes in braincase geometry. Notably, rotation of the occiput toward a ventral orientation is associated with important changes to SCC shape that match those observed during the dinosaur–bird transition. This suggests that evolutionary transformations of SCC shape during the Mesozoic origin of avian flight resulted from evolutionary changes in the orientation of the craniocervical joint, and not from tuning of SCC sensory function. These findings illuminate the importance of integrated morphological changes to the head-neck system during bird origins and challenge the long-standing assumption that SCC morphology enables confident inferences of the locomotor capabilities of…

items.title: Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees
items.summary_raw: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system’s strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model’s ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

items.title: A moveable feast: Neurons become less picky eaters after hibernation
Structural insights into the coupling mechanism of vectorial CO 2 uptake by DAB1
items.summary_raw: CO 2 transporters enable bacterial CO 2 -concentrating mechanisms by catalyzing directional hydration of CO 2 , yet the basis of this vectorial carbonic anhydrase (CA) activity remains an open question. We used cryoelectron microscopy to determine the structure of the DAB1 complex from Thermocrinis albus to 2.29 Å, revealing a heterotrimer in which a deeply buried β-CA active site in DabA is structurally coupled to the proton-translocating subunit DabB. Two conformational states define distinct solvent channels for substrate entry and product exit. A suppressor screen identifies mutations that disrupt coupling while retaining CA activity, underlying the importance of conserved residues that link proton translocation to active-site remodeling. These results support a model in which proton-driven conformational changes regulate substrate access to the active site, enabling vectorial CO 2 hydration.

items.title: Nonclassical growth to mesoporous quasi-single crystal CeO 2 superstructures with a well-defined surface
items.summary_raw: Single-crystal materials are essential for fundamental catalysis studies and advanced technologies; however, synthesizing single crystals that simultaneously integrate mesoporosity, tunable size, and well-defined surfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a wet-chemical, template-free strategy to synthesize mesoporous quasi-single-crystal CeO 2 superparticles (SPs). Operando wide- and small-angle X-ray scattering combined with theoretical modeling reveal a nonclassical growth mechanism driven by the oriented attachment of nanocluster building blocks. This process yields high-surface-area quasi-single crystals that preferentially expose energetically favorable (111) facets on both the external surfaces and internal pore walls, thereby enhancing the stabilization of active sites when used as heterogeneous catalyst supports. Using this approach, we demonstrate broad applicability by synthesizing highly dispersed precious metal–loaded CeO 2 (M/CeO 2 , M = Pd, Pt, Rh, or Ir) and metal-doped CeO 2 (Cu–CeO 2 ) SPs. Moreover, Pd/CeO 2 SPs exhibit effective stabilization of Pd clusters in CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol, delivering a high methanol selectivity of 85% and markedly improved durability compared with conventional supports.

items.title: Improved assessment of Alaskan Arctic coastal wave exposure accounting for landfast ice
items.summary_raw: Simulations of the ocean wave climate are critical for assessment of coastal processes and hazards in observation sparse regions such as the Arctic. While the multidecade wind and ice datasets necessary for driving long-term wave simulations have proven reliable for such efforts, the presence of landfast ice along shorelines at scales not represented by these data has been a persistent uncertainty impeding accurate analysis of impacts to Arctic coasts. Here, we explore this uncertainty by producing a historical high-resolution wave simulation and combining simulation outputs with landfast ice data for the Alaskan Arctic. The resulting dataset yields an improved assessment of coastal waves and identifies stark contrasts in the seasonal wave exposure of the Chukchi and Beaufort regions. Notably, analysis shows that absent supplemented landfast ice, coastal ice cover is broadly underestimated by 10 to 25 d, resulting in wave energy being overestimated by 5 to 10% in shallow depths nearshore. Notably, these figures can reach up to 70 d of underestimation for ice cover and 48% overestimation of wave energy in certain locations. The persistent overestimation and potential for extreme positive biases in coastal wave assessment highlight the need for representation of landfast ice in Arctic coastal analysis efforts and our analysis reveals the spatial and temporal biases for related research.

items.title: Correction for Pan et al., SNHG26 orchestrates pro-fibrotic fibroblast maintenance via PTBP1-mediated alternative polyadenylation of AKT3 in dermal fibrosis
Shedding light on left hippocampal mGlu5 in Alzheimer’s disease
items.summary_raw: Metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGlu5) is essential for synaptic plasticity and memory, making it a potential therapeutic target in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). While hemispheric asymmetries in hippocampal function have been observed in AD patients, the lateralized contribution of mGlu5 signaling to cognitive decline remains unclear. Here, we show a physiological left-right asymmetry in hippocampal mGlu5 expression in wild-type mice, with higher levels in the left hemisphere, consistent with previous reports. This physiological asymmetry is lost in two distinct mouse models of AD, the J20 and 5xFAD mice, revealing a hemisphere-specific disruption of hippocampal mGlu5 regulation. Using the light-controllable negative allosteric modulator Alloswitch-1, we show that selective inhibition of left, but not right, hippocampal mGlu5 restores working and short-term memory in AD mice. This finding indicates that altered mGlu5 expression does not simply reflect receptor loss, but rather a dysregulated signaling state that remains functionally relevant and pharmacologically targetable. Left-specific modulation also normalizes pathological downstream signaling, including aberrant Pyk2 and GSK-3β activation and tau hyperphosphorylation, across both hemispheres, indicating a widespread impact of hemisphere-selective intervention. These findings establish a functional lateralization of hippocampal mGlu5 signaling and identify the left hippocampus as a critical site for mGlu5-dependent…

items.title: Invariances in an ever-variant environment
Heterochronicity shapes brain network formation
items.summary_raw: Brain network formation unfolds on a nonuniform developmental timetable, with different cortical regions generating connections at different developmental phases. Generative network models (GNMs) aim to uncover the principles underpinning the organization of connectomes by creating synthetic networks according to simple computational rules. These models capture the connectome’s topology, operationalized here as the cumulative distributions of network metrics (e.g., modularity, small-worldness, rich-club structure). However, GNMs typically ignore the differential timing of connectivity formation, and by omitting this temporal programme they often misplace topological features in physical space. Here, we add a heterochronous growth term to GNMs and use a model fitness function that weighs topology and topography equally. Topography refers to the spatial embedding of the network—the actual anatomical positions of the axonal tracts. With these advances, we can generate synthetic networks that more faithfully reproduce the spatial layout of diffusion-MRI connectomes from two independent adult cohorts. Compared with classical, temporally agnostic models, heterochronous simulations improve model fit, accurately locate cortical hubs and modules across individuals, and converge on a single caudal-to-rostral gradient of brain maturation. Overall, integrating heterochronicity makes GNMs more faithful to brain development, and allows for better identification of individual differences…

items.title: In mice, a population of male germ cells shows characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest
items.summary_raw: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male’s reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.

items.title: Evolution shapes ecosystem resilience through spatial self-organization
items.summary_raw: Drylands are globally widespread and ecologically important but vulnerable to climate change. Many exhibit spatially self-organized vegetation patterns that enhance resilience by enabling vegetation to reorganize their patterns under drying, thereby optimizing water use and maintaining productivity. Plants can also undergo evolution in response to environmental change. Although both spatial self-organization and rapid evolution are fundamental mechanisms of resilience, their interaction remains largely unknown. Using a theoretical model, we examine how these mechanisms interact to shape vegetation transitions—abrupt or gradual—and ecosystem resilience under climatic drying. We find that pattern formation can suppress adaptation by maintaining soil moisture beneath vegetation patches despite rainfall decline, thereby limiting selection for increased drought tolerance. However, this suppression is largely alleviated under the variable rainfall typical of drylands. In turn, evolution feeds back on self-organization by increasing the spatial plasticity of vegetation patterns and their ability to reorganize under changing climate, although this positive effect weakens as evolutionary rate increases. Considering direct (adaptation) and indirect (pattern-mediated) effects, evolution enhances resilience, with indirect effects via pattern plasticity dominating. Within model scenarios spanning plausible rainfall variability and relative evolutionary-to-ecological rates, more than half…

items.title: Direct physical contacts with epithelial cells regulate leukocyte actin dynamics to facilitate intraepithelial motility in vivo
items.summary_raw: Efficient immune cell migration requires physical interactions with surrounding tissues. While tissue matrix mechanics influence leukocyte motility, it is unknown how leukocytes exert pushing and pulling forces to traverse cell-dense epithelial tissues in vivo. Here, we leverage the optical transparency of larval zebrafish to identify how physical interactions with epithelial cells regulate mechanisms of neutrophil force generation to navigate cell-dense tissues. Confining forces from epithelial cells induce a mechanosensitive central actin network, mediated by Cdc42 and Wiskott–Aldrich Syndrome Protein, which exerts expansile forces on surrounding cells to dilate a path for migration. In concert, direct cell-to-cell (leukocyte–epithelial) contacts mediated by integrin ɑE recognition of epithelial cadherin generate traction forces to enable forward motility. Together, our findings identify how physical interactions with the surrounding cellular environment regulate leukocyte motility through epithelial tissue in vivo.

items.title: Climate tools without climate consensus: weather and climate decision support tools create openings for agricultural adaptation
items.summary_raw: Abstract Despite the investment in climate and weather decision support tools and services, their adoption is reported to be lower than expected. Even with advances in modeling and forecasting, these tools are underutilized in agricultural decision-making. Historically, it has been widely assumed that concern with rapidly occurring climate change was a precursor to climate adaptation within the agricultural sector. Emerging research, including this study, challenges the coupling between climate change belief and adaptive action. Drawing on survey data from more than 383 California farmers and ranchers and 121 agricultural advisors, we find no statistically significant relationship between our Climate Concern Index—a measure that integrates belief with related dimensions of evidence, attribution, motivation and interest in learning—and the use of climate decision support tools by farmers and ranchers. We also identify a sharp epistemological divide: while most producers reported having sufficient information to manage climate risks, advisors overwhelmingly believed that producers lacked it, reflecting differing standards for what counts as ‘enough’ knowledge. We argue that climate decision support tools act as boundary objects: common instruments that support coordination among users with varied perspectives, without needing agreement on the causes of climate change. In doing so, we posit that they may also shape mental models of climate variability and change over time…

items.summary_raw: The ocean surrounding California’s Channel Islands can feel like another world. Beneath the surface sway towering kelp forests that are patrolled by huge sheephead fish, striking in pink and black with protruding teeth, along with refrigerator-sized giant sea bass. Seals and sea lions swim among colorful sponges and sea stars. “We sometimes think of the Channel Islands as our Galapagos in California,” said Doug McCauley, a professor of marine science at UC Santa Barbara. The cornucopia of marine wildlife here wasn’t always this vibrant. Violet Sage Walker, the chair of California’s Northern Chumash Tribal Council, recalled documentary footage showing the Channel Islands before marine protections were enacted, in an era when intensive commercial fishing had damaged kelp forests and key species. “It looked like Mars, like a dead planet,” she said. But beginning in 2003, areas around the Channel Islands were designated as California Marine Protected Areas, or MPAs — a conservation strategy akin to creating underwater state parks . With roughly 150 square miles of protected waters, the islands now function as a safe haven for marine flora and fauna, essentially acting as nurseries for baby fish and protecting dozens of iconic species like kelp bass, rockfish, leopard sharks, and more. items.title: Jared Huffman Wants to See Some Changes to the Senate’s Permitting Bill
items.summary_raw: The most important voice in Congress criticizing the Senate’s bipartisan energy permitting deal is Representative Jared Huffman. A California Democrat who previously worked in environmental legal advocacy, Huffman has long been among the most impassioned lawmakers on climate issues. Under the first Trump administration, his voice was often the loudest calling for oversight and accountability on energy and climate policy. Under the second Trump administration, he has been a spirited defender of offshore wind . Should Democrats take control of the U.S. House of Representatives in the coming midterm elections, as expected, then Huffman is first in line to become chair of the lower chamber’s Natural Resources Committee. This makes him one of the few people able to armchair quarterback permitting talks in Congress right now. The proposed legislation currently on the table, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, would fundamentally reshape how federal project permitting happens. It would constrain National Environmental Policy Act reviews. It would radically alter transmission approvals. It would let companies sue the government for damages if they can show that an agency was unduly discriminating against them based on fuel type. It would limit state and tribal authority to object against projects under the Clean Water Act. And it would make this whole process more transparent by instituting digital reporting requirements. items.title: A slice of Toast for everyone: Supporting ontological security and wellbeing through a not-for-profit energy hardship intervention
items.summary_raw: Energy hardship is a multi-dimensional and structurally produced condition that shapes health, wellbeing, relationships, and the ability to experience the home as a place of safety and stability. Drawing on the theory of ontological security, we examine how energy hardship disrupts everyday life and how integrated energy support can alleviate these harms. We present qualitative findings from 21 semi-structured interviews with customers of Toast Electric, Aotearoa New Zealand's first not-for-profit electricity retailer run by a charitable organisation, on the Energy Wellbeing Programme. Through thematic analysis, we found that high energy costs and poor housing quality generated chronic stress, forced trade-offs between heating and other essentials, undermined health management, and disrupted family dynamics. Participation in the Energy Wellbeing Programme reduced bill-related anxiety, enabled more adequate heating use, and strengthened wellbeing at individual, household, and wider family levels. Crucially, these benefits arose not from improving energy affordability alone, but from the programme's integrated and relational approach, combining discounted energy, tailored energy advice through home visits, and connections to housing improvement programmes. We argue that energy hardship interventions must move beyond single-solution approaches and instead adopt people-centred, structural models that simultaneously address energy affordability and housing quality alongside…

items.summary_raw: This study aims to evaluate and prioritize clean energy strategies to support Türkiye's national carbon neutrality goals. Achieving carbon neutrality requires adopting clean technologies and effective environmental policy tools. This study presents a novel multi-criteria decision-making context that combines the Picture Fuzzy Best-Worst Method (PiF-BWM) and Picture Fuzzy Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (PiF-TOPSIS) to evaluate and prioritize renewable energy strategies under uncertainty systematically. The empirical application focuses on Türkiye and is based on the evaluations of nine experts. Using Türkiye as the test bed, we assess alternatives such as climate-resilient low-carbon development plans, policy frameworks for low-carbon fuels, large-scale and distributed renewables, green jobs programs, and building electrification via heat pumps. Criteria span environmental impact, cost and financial viability, technological feasibility, socioeconomic effects, resilience, energy efficiency, energy security, and policy alignment. The methodology first applies PiF-BWM to determine the criteria weights, and then uses PiF-TOPSIS to rank the alternative strategies. Results show that environmentally effective and policy-enabled strategies deliver the highest urban decarbonization benefits, while building-focused electrification provides targeted gains when integrated with local grid constraints and building codes. items.title: How the European economic area electricity trading market failed into Gresham's Law dynamics and how to redesign it
items.summary_raw: The current European Economic Area electricity trading was established to lower retail prices and secure the supply of power to its customers. However, the results are the opposite. Prices have increased and the supply of power has become less stable after the integration of variable renewable energy sources, such as solar photovoltaics and wind power. The failure to account for the fact that power from intermittent energy sources differs fundamentally in quality from the power generated by dispatchable energy sources has transformed the trading system into one governed by Gresham's Law. Also, the system has changed its behavior from complicated and probabilistic to complex and uncertain due to the covariation in weather patterns over large swaths of land. The result is growing market volatility and escalating costs. A major part of the uncertainty associated with this complexity is ontological. The proposed improvements to the risk management of the power grid are insufficient and may make the situation worse because it suggests that there is, contrary to findings in complexity science, a solution to ontological uncertainty. This paper is novel in using Gresham's Law and complexity science, and it proposes two new rules for the trading system to drive the power grid away from Gresham's Law dynamics. items.title: Non-price barriers to the development of electromobility with an aspect of regional disparities

The research is focused on identifying non-price barriers in order to find out what are the most important non-price barriers to faster/more dynamic development of electromobility, what policies the Czech Republic has in place to meet its climate goals in the transition to zero-emission mobility, and what is the degree of consistency between the applied policies and the identified barriers and whether there are or how significant regional disparities are from the perspective of households. The aim of the article is to introduce selected non-price barriers to the development of electromobility, to clarify how the barriers are perceived by residents and to define the differences according to the size of the municipality in which they live. items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.summary_raw: The growing demand for reliable and sustainable energy sources in Nigeria has intensified the need to explore renewable alternatives that can address the limitations of conventional fossil fuel-based systems. This study aimed to assess the feasibility, performance, and socio environmental impacts of implementing a Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) that combines solar photovoltaic (PV) and biomass energy resources as an efficient and eco friendly power generation option for Omoku Town. The research employed an integrated engineering and simulation-based approach using resource data such as global horizontal irradiance (GHI), biomass residue estimates, and load demand profiles. Monthly solar radiation data indicated an average GHI of 4.77 kWh/m²/day and a clearness index of 0.49, suggesting consistent solar availability throughout the year. Biomass resource assessment revealed an estimated 27,500 tons of biomass residues annually, comprising cassava peels, palm kernel shells, sawdust, and agricultural wastes, capable of generating approximately 28,380 MWh/year. Using the HOMER Pro software, the optimal hybrid configuration was determined to consist of a 40 MW solar PV array, a 25 MW biomass power plant, 100 MWh of battery storage, and a 10 MW grid backup system, generating a total of 157,760 MWh/year. The energy mix achieved a renewable fraction of 87.3%, with biomass and solar contributing 47.2% and 40.1% of the total supply, respectively. Economically, the HRES…

items.title: Children at the Frontline of Climate Change: A Vulnerability-Based Assessment of Climate Impacts on Children in Afghanistan
items.summary_raw: Background: Afghanistan ranks among the world's most climate-vulnerable nations, yet rigorous, peer-reviewed analysis of climate change impacts specifically on children has remained severely underexplored. Children in Afghanistan face a convergence of acute physiological vulnerability, structural deprivation, governance failure, and compounding humanitarian crises that render them disproportionately exposed to climate hazards including drought, extreme temperatures, flash flooding, and food insecurity. Methods: This study employs a systematic integrative review combining scoping review methodology with secondary vulnerability analysis. A total of 323 records were identified across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and major institutional repositories; 145 sources met inclusion criteria (peer-reviewed studies, institutional reports, and official datasets published between 2018 and 2025 that contain empirical data on children in Afghanistan). Vulnerability is operationalized across five interlinked dimensions: biophysical exposure, nutritional and health status, water and sanitation access, educational continuity, and social protection. A Child-Centered Climate Vulnerability Index for Afghanistan (CCVI-Af) is developed and pillar weights are justified against established global indices. Results: Afghanistan registered the highest absolute number of children displaced by climate disasters globally in 2023 (n = 747,094). Newborns face a projected 5.3-times greater…

items.title: Land carbon sinks in the European Union are not keeping pace with carbon neutrality expectations
items.summary_raw: Abstract The European Union has substantially reduced greenhouse-gas emissions since 1990, yet the land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sink has not strengthened in parallel. The EU-27 LULUCF balance was approximately −231 MtCO₂e in 2024, while the latest Member State projections indicate a remaining gap of 40–55 MtCO₂e to the binding −310 MtCO₂e target for 2030. Here, we synthesise recent assessments to examine the drivers of this weakening in the land carbon sink and their implications for the effectiveness of climate mitigation policy. Declining forest growth, increased harvesting, climate-driven disturbances, and rising biomass demand reduce net carbon uptake, with one 2040 GLOBIOM sensitivity analysis indicating an approximately 100 MtCO₂e reduction in the LULUCF sink under an additional 20 Mtoe of woody-biomass demand. Concurrently, the EU inventory reported 52.7% uncertainty in the 2022 LULUCF level and 29.4% uncertainty in its trend, while important soil-carbon dynamics remain incompletely represented. These findings indicate that current climate policy frameworks implicitly assume stable, scalable, and rapidly deliverable land-based removals, whereas land carbon sinks are dynamic, disturbance-sensitive, and constrained by biophysical limits. Addressing this mismatch requires land-removal plans to be evaluated through dependable removal capacity, combining expected annual net removal with stock change, delivery time, inventory uncertainty, disturbance and…

items.title: Governments or facilitators? Power and politics of multi-level sustainable energy governance in Surat, Gujarat
items.summary_raw: Urban areas are becoming strategic sites in the ongoing sustainable energy transition, driven by the new opportunities and imperatives presented by decentralized sustainable energy technologies. However, the presence of cities in the global clean energy landscape remains underwhelming. Despite national programs encouraging urban energy transition in India, the response has largely failed to meet the goals. The existing literature has primarily attributed this to a lack of technical and financial capacity and to the limited legislative role of urban governments. This paper deepens these arguments and offers a more layered view through the case study of Surat in Gujarat, India. I argue that India’s clean energy transition is unfolding within the traditional frameworks and templates that propped up the conventional energy systems, entrenching incumbent power hierar chies. Increasing institutionalization is leading to increased centralization, narrowing the scope of participation for newer actors, including local urban governments. Surat’s case study demonstrates that city governments are keen to respond to local challenges by capitalizing on the opportunities presented by sustainable energy sources. However, the enduring success of their initiatives will depend on supportive agential, structural, and institutional reforms initiated by the powerful elites within India’s energy governance landscape.

items.title: Development trends and driving mechanisms of coordination in the Digitalization–Urban development–low-carbon transition system
items.summary_raw: Against the backdrop of sustainable development and China’s Dual Carbon Goals, Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition continuously interact to shape urban sustainable development. However, the long-term coordination of the Digitalization–Urban Development–Low-carbon Transition (DUL) system and its underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. To address this research gap, using panel data for 289 prefecture-level and above cities in China from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs the DUL system and applies the CRITIC-Entropy Weight Method to evaluate the development levels of the three subsystems and the overall DUL system. The Local and Tele-coupling Coordination Degree (LTCCD) is employed to characterize long-term coordination, while the Dagum Gini coefficient and GeoDetector are used to examine regional disparities and driving mechanisms. Based on this analytical framework, the results show that: (1) the development levels of Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition all improved continuously, but their evolutionary trajectories differed, resulting in asynchronous development of the DUL system; (2) LTCCD exhibited a sustained upward trend, with coordination gradually evolving from imbalance to coordination, although eastern China consistently outperformed the central and western regions; (3) regional disparities in LTCCD generally narrowed, while interregional differences remained the primary source of spatial disparities…

items.title: Belief-sensitive norm nudging for household tap water use: an indirect-pathways argument
items.summary_raw: Norm-based nudges are increasingly used to promote environmentally responsible behavior, including more sustainable water use. It is widely recognized that such interventions should be informed by prior survey-based research. A more specific and often neglected question, however, concerns what those surveys should actually measure. This article addresses that question in the case of household tap-water use. We argue, first, that social norms often influence behavior not only directly but also indirectly, through mediating constructs such as personal norms, attitudes toward the behavior, and perceived behavioral control. Second, drawing on the Reasoned Action Approach and related work on mediated norm effects, we argue that these constructs are grounded in underlying behavioral, normative, and control beliefs. Accordingly, surveys designed to inform norm-based interventions should not focus primarily on self-reported behavior alone, but should also identify the belief patterns through which normative influence is likely to operate in a given population. On this basis, we propose a belief-sensitive survey blueprint for household tap-water use. The paper's contribution is therefore not to advance a new general theory of norm nudging, but to clarify how an indirect-pathways perspective can inform the design of more context-sensitive and belief-sensitive water interventions.

items.title: BETWEEN FARMERS' VOICES AND THE GOVERNMENT'S IMAGE:FOOD SECURITY NARRATIVES IN LAMPUNG'S LOCAL MEDIA (2021–2025)
items.summary_raw: This study analyzes the response of local media in Lampung Province to the issue of food security through news. Using thematic analysis, this study examines news from seven local media—TVRI Lampung, Lampung Post, RMOL Lampung, Antara, Tribunlampung, Radar Lampung, and Konsentris—in the 2021–2025 period. The findings show a diverse framing pattern. Government media (TVRI Lampung and Antara) consistently frame food security as an issue that has been successfully addressed through government programs, emphasizing production and modernization, and limiting critical voices. Independent media (Lampung Post, Tribunlampung, RMOL Lampung, Radar Lampung, and Konsentris) present a more diverse frame, highlighting policy failures, farmers' difficulties, environmental crises, and structural poverty. This creates a fragmented public discourse, where audiences accessing different media have different understandings of the reality of food security. The media serves as information providers, policy watchdogs, community empowerment, government narrative balancers, and agents of social change. However, news is still descriptive, reactive, and event-focused, lacking in digging into the root causes of problems and long-term solutions. This study recommends increasing the depth and sustainability of news, diversifying sources, strengthening media independence, and cross-sector collaboration. Comparisons with global experiences in Nigeria, Kenya, Ethiopia, and Algeria offer valuable lessons for…

Why support for net-zero technologies can be politically vulnerable: Evidence from Celtic Sea floating offshore wind
items.summary_raw: Support for net-zero technologies can be broad yet remain politically vulnerable. Actors may converge on the same technology through distinct problem diagnoses without forming a resilient coalition. This Perspectives article examines this proposition through Celtic Sea floating offshore wind (FLOW), a less mature and more expensive technology than fixed-foundation offshore wind. It draws on 68 interviews conducted primarily in 2024 with actors involved in or adjacent to FLOW development. Because opponents and affected publics were not interviewed, the interview material provides an ex-ante baseline rather than a reconstruction of contestation. This baseline is interpreted retrospectively through Hajer's discourse-coalition framework, supported by Ford and Newell's account of regime accommodation and Jasanoff and Kim's socio-technical imaginaries. The analysis identifies four problems for which FLOW was presented as an appropriate response: limitations of existing technologies and deployment geographies in delivering net-zero electricity at scale; vulnerability arising from fossil-fuel dependence and geographic concentration; industrial decline and uneven regional development; and the risk of losing commercial position in an emerging global market. Although these diagnoses differed, each made FLOW appear appropriate, creating an emerging FLOW-supportive discursive alignment rather than a consolidated discourse coalition. This discursive breadth created political flexibility…

items.title: Consequential life cycle assessment of agricultural products: state of the art and research needs
items.source_name: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
items.summary_raw: Abstract Purpose Consequential Life Cycle Assessment (cLCA) was developed to assess large-scale consequences, supporting applications like policy-making. Unlike the well-established attributional approach, cLCA is characterized by lower maturity. Specifically, a lack of consensus on the identification of marginal data, system boundary setting and handling of results’ uncertainties impedes its practical use. We examine how agricultural cLCA studies handle these methodological challenges, focusing on food and biobased materials. Methods A systematic literature review was carried out, initially yielding 229 cLCA studies. The eligibility screening led to the final selection of 23 studies on biobased materials and 32 studies on food. These were primarily analysed regarding marginal data identification, system boundary setting, and uncertainty assessment, alongside supplementary methodological aspects, such as functional unit, use of market models, study scope, and reasoning for consequential modelling. Results and Discussion The review identified a broad variety of approaches for addressing methodological challenges of cLCA, without significant differences between biobased materials and food, while revealing documentation gaps and inconsistencies in reported methodological procedures. Marginal data identification relied mostly on ecoinvent consequential and formalized guidelines, while 11% of the studies did not specify the procedure. Around a third reported using market models…

items.title: My house, my car, my footprint: A sustainable consumption corridor analysis of Nordic households
items.summary_raw: This study operationalizes a ‘Corridor Framework’ to study sustainable consumption for the housing-mobility nexus across the Nordic countries. Survey data containing socio-demographic and consumption patterns of 6694 households was used to estimate consumption and consumption-based carbon footprints for these households. Emission and dynamic minimum consumption thresholds were applied from the literature to develop the corridor and applied to the dataset to a distributional corridor analysis. We found a general high level of emission overshoot alongside widespread high achievement above the minimum consumption threshold, in line with expectations for high-income, high-equality countries, though income-based inequalities in consumption and emissions existed. One key finding was that rather than trade-offs between mobility and housing, as income rose, consumption and emissions rose together, likely pointing to needs-satisfier escalation and positional consumption. Second, infrastructural emissions intensities are heterogeneously locking-in a high percentage of household personas, where even at the minimum consumption level, they would still be in a state of emission overshoot. Examples include rural households in Denmark, Finland, and Iceland where 60%+ are locked out of the mobility corridor or urban housing Denmark and Finland 70–80% due to high‑carbon energy sources. items.title: An integrated model of climate and environmental pathways to violent extremism
items.summary_raw: Climate change and violent extremism represent intersecting global threats, yet their relationship remains under-examined. This preregistered systematic review synthesizes 45 studies across disciplines to develop an integrated conceptual model of climate-extremism pathways based on the current literature. Our synthesis shows that climate variability correlates with terrorist attack frequency, climate shocks create governance vacuums exploited by extremist organizations, environmental degradation fuels extremist narratives, and climate threat cues increase authoritarian attitudes and out-group hostility. These pathways are moderated by various factors including state capacity, community resilience, and pre-existing ideologies. Our proposed Integrative Climate-Extremism Model distinguishes between extremist endorsement (attitudinal support), advocacy (recruitment and propaganda), willingness (behavioral intentions), and execution (violent acts), outlining how each is influenced by different pathways. This synthesis reveals climate change as a threat multiplier rather than direct cause of violent extremism, operating through material, institutional, psychological, and ideological mechanisms. We identify critical research gaps, propose targeted interventions to disrupt climate-extremism pathways, and discuss anticipatory governance strategies.

items.title: The Role of Renewable Energy in Rural Development: Insights from a 1KVA Fuel-less Generator Design
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.summary_raw: The integration of renewable energy sources in rural development initiatives has gained significant attention as a sustainable solution to energy poverty and economic stagnation in remote areas. This paper delves into the role of a 1KVA fuel-less generator project as a case study to demonstrate the potential of renewable energy in transforming rural communities. The project, designed to harness clean energy without reliance on conventional fuels, addresses the pressing need for reliable and affordable power in regions where access to the national grid is either limited or nonexistent. The study explores the technical specifications of the 1KVA fuel-less generator, its operational efficiency, and its adaptability to various rural settings. Beyond the technological aspects, the research investigates the socio-economic impact of deploying such generators, highlighting improvements in local livelihoods, increased productivity, and enhanced quality of life. Furthermore, the environmental benefits of the fuel-less generator, such as the reduction of carbon emissions and decreased dependency on fossil fuels, are critically analyzed. By drawing on field data and community feedback, the paper underscores the importance of stakeholder engagement, capacity building, and policy support in the successful implementation of renewable energy projects in rural areas.
